嘉靖八年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖八年三月初十日，禮部尚書臣李時等於奉天門奏：「為科舉事，會試天下舉人，取中三百二十名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士楊一清等五十七員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光祿大夫、左柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士楊一清，壬辰進士。

光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太傅、吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士張璁，辛巳進士。

光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太傅、吏部尚書、武英殿大學士桂萼，辛未進士。

光祿大夫、柱國、太子太保、吏部尚書兼翰林院學士方獻夫，乙丑進士。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Eighth Year of Jiajing (1529)

Imperial Words

On the tenth day of the third month of the eighth year of Jiajing, your servant Li Shi, Minister of Rites, and others memorialized at the Fengtian Gate: “Concerning the civil-service examinations: the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm has selected 320 successful candidates. The Palace Examination will be held on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year. We accordingly request the appointment of fifty-seven officials as Readers and other examination functionaries, including Yang Yiqing, Junior Preceptor concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The classes of metropolitan graduate status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class shall, as customary, comprise three men. The first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with all three granted metropolitan graduate status ‘with honors.’ The second class shall receive rank 7b and be granted metropolitan graduate status. The third class shall receive rank 8a and be granted status equivalent to that of metropolitan graduates.” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respect this.

Readers

Yang Yiqing held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement, Left Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. He was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Zhang Cong held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Gui E held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Fang Xianfu held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Zhai Luan held the prestige title Grand Master for Assisting in Governance and was Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Liang Cai was Minister of Revenue and a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.

Gao Youji held the prestige title Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and was Minister of Justice. He was a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.

Liu Lin held the prestige title Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and was Minister of Works. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.

Xiong Jia was Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Huo Tao held the prestige title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and was Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Song Cang held the prestige title Grand Master for Upholding the Constitution and was Left Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission. He was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Mu Konghui held the prestige title Grand Master for Administrative Service and was Left Companion (zuo shuzi) in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Xu Chengming was Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and held the prestige title Grand Master for Straightforward Service. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Zhang Chao was Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and held the prestige title Grand Master for Straightforward Service. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Xi Chun was Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and held the prestige title Grand Master for Promoting Instruction. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Yan Song held the prestige title Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and was Right Vice Minister of Rites. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Zhao Dui held the prestige title Gentleman for Scholarly Excellence and was Investigating Censor for the Yunnan Circuit. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

The eighth year of Jiajing (1529).

Early on the fifteenth day of the third month, the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy questions.

Early on the nineteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. On this day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial regalia on the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation of examination results, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate. Once the proclamation had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-ranked graduate back to his residence with a ceremonial parasol and retinue.

On the twentieth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…A banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. When the banquet ended, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate was granted court robes, a cap, and a belt, and the metropolitan graduates were granted paper currency.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for the imperial favor.
On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
The Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names.

第一甲三名，賜進士及第。

羅洪先〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字達夫，行五，年二十六，十月十四日生〕。曾祖良〔衛經歷〕，祖玉〔贈兵部員外郎〕，父循〔按察司副使〕，母李氏〔加封宜人〕。具慶下，弟壽先、居先，娶曾氏。江西鄉試第八十名，會試第二十六名。

程文德〔貫浙江金華府永康縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字舜敷，行八十四，年三十三，九月初三日生〕。曾祖永延，祖世剛〔封南京大理寺右評事〕，父銈〔按察司副使〕，母趙氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄文思，弟文謨、文訓，娶潘氏。浙江鄉試第八名，會試第十名。

楊名〔貫四川潼川州遂寧縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字實卿，行二，年二十五，六月十四日生〕。曾祖萬全〔壽官〕，祖時景〔壽官〕，父洪江，母杜氏。重慶下，弟台，娶劉氏。四川鄉試第一名，會試第六十九名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Luo Hongxian, registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Dafu; he ranked fifth in family order, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Liang was a Guard Registrar; his grandfather Yu was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of War; his father Xun was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Li, received the additional title of Lady of Suitability (yiren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shouxian and Juxian, and his wife was née Zeng. He placed eightieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Wende, registered in a civilian household in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shunfu; he ranked eighty-fourth in family order, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongyan; his grandfather Shigang was granted the title of Right Case Reviewer in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review; his father Ji was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Zhao, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wensi, his younger brothers were Wenmo and Wenxun, and his wife was née Pan. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ming, registered in a civilian household in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shiqing; he ranked second in family order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Wanquan and grandfather Shijing both held honorary official titles conferred for longevity; his father was Hongjiang, and his mother was née Du. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brother was Tai, and his wife was née Liu. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety-five men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Tang Shunzhi, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingde. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yan was posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; his grandfather Gui held that office. His father Yao was a tribute scholar, and his mother was née Ren. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhengzhi, and his wife was née Zhuang. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shu, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuezhi. He ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Qu was a Police Chief; his grandfather was Yue, and his father was Lianqing. His mother was née Qi. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Mo and Jian, and he was betrothed to a woman née Dong. He placed seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Han, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Xichong County. He was a student at the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaohai. He ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather Gongrong was a County Vice Magistrate, and his father Jiuding was a County Registrar. His mother was née Jia. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Song, a student at the Directorate of Education, Jiang, Lan, and Yangzhi. His wife was née Hua. He placed thirteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Jiezhi, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yinhe; he ranked fourth in birth order and was twenty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Quezong; his grandfather, Yu; his father, Kun; and his mother, née Liao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing and Xian, and he married a woman née Liang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jing, registered in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongfu; he ranked fourth in birth order and was forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Ke, a student of the Imperial University; his father, Qi; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ziya, a prefectural Clerk; his younger brothers were Gan, Yue, Kuang, and Jiang. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently women née Peng and née Jiang. He placed fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Bao, registered in Yiyang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, in a household registered for horse-transport boat service, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Chushan; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty, born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Mengzhao; his grandfather, Gong; his father, Wanling, an honorary official; and his mother, née Xiao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin; his younger brothers were Bi and Yu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lianfang, registered in Xunyang County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household and originally from Jishui County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Boshi; he ranked sixth in birth order and was twenty-five, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Fuyou; his grandfather, Erding; his father, Heng, a student of the Imperial University; and his mother, née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lianhui; his younger brothers were Lianbi, Lianzhi, Xianfang, and Liancai. He married a woman née Xie. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Kui 何煃 was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he had the courtesy name Zishi, ranked fifth in his family, and was aged thirty, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yongan; his grandfather, Chang, was a District Magistrate; and his father, Kui 逵, was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His father's former wives were Lady Chen, posthumously honored as Lady for Service, and Lady Ou; his mother was Lady Zhao, also posthumously honored as Lady for Service. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hong, a District Magistrate; Hui; Ao, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Qiu. His younger brothers were Fang and Chang. He married Lady Yu. He placed fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yinglin 栗應麟 was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Shanxi. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Renfu, ranked first in his family, and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, was granted the honorary title Wenlin lang; his grandfather, Zhen, was a Food Service Officer; his father, Rong, was a Consort; and his mother was the County Princess of Guiping. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingfang, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Yingshao. His younger brothers were Yingkui, a tribute scholar; Yingpeng; Yingkui [the name is repeated in the transcription: ?]; Yingzhi; Yingke; Yingqiu; and Yingqi. He married Lady Song. He placed twenty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Huai 盧淮 was registered in a military household of Huai'an Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he had the courtesy name Beiji, ranked first in his family, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather, Rong, held an honorary office awarded for public generosity; his grandfather was Lian; his father, Gao, held an honorary office awarded for longevity; and his mother was Lady Sang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing and Yuan; his younger brothers were Hong, Hai, Zi, and Hui. He married Lady Chen. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xueyi 王學益 was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Yuqing, ranked forty-seventh in his family, and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Xunji, and grandfather, Min, both held honorary offices awarded for longevity. His father, Jia, was granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his mother, Lady Yan, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xuesheng, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; Xuekong, a Prefectural Judge; Xuelong; Xueshun, a tribute scholar; and Xuewu, a tribute scholar. He married Lady Liu. He placed forty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

重慶下　弟懷義　懷禮　懷智　聘陳氏

朱麟〔貫江西吉安府萬安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子仁，行四，年四十，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖元飾，祖祖貴〔義官〕，父憲〔訓導〕，母劉氏，繼母徐氏。具慶下，兄鸞、鵬〔順天舉人〕、鶴〔監生〕、鵷〔陰陽正術〕，弟鷹，娶李氏，繼娶康氏。江西鄉試第十七名，會試第一百九名。

鄭絅〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，軍籍，府學附學生，治書經，字子尚，行五，年二十九，十月十六日生〕。曾祖商〔壽官〕，祖崇，父瓚〔户部主事〕，母陳氏。永感下，兄大賓、大同〔同科進士〕，弟約、奮、紹、大河、紱、緋，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十二名，會試第四十三名。

梁懷仁〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字宅之，行一，年二十，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖隆，祖武榮，父黼，母莊氏。重慶下，弟懷義、懷禮、懷智，聘陳氏。福建鄉試第六十四名，會試第十四名。
translation_en:
Xiang Qiao, registered in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a wealthy-household registration category and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Qianzhi. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ang, his grandfather Yuan, his father Shi, and his mother née Lou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ge, Cai, and Zi. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Lin, registered in Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziren. Fourth in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanshi; his grandfather Zugui held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his father Xian was an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Luan, Peng (a provincial graduate of Shuntian), He (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Yuan (Director of the School of Yin and Yang); his younger brother was Ying. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Kang. He ranked seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Jiong, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zishang. Fifth in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shang held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Chong; his father Zan was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dabin and Datong (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort); his younger brothers were Yue, Fen, Shao, Dahe, Fu, and Fei. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Huairen, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhaizhi. First in birth order, he was aged twenty and was born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Long, his grandfather Wurong, his father Fu, and his mother née Zhuang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Huaiyi, Huaili, and Huaizhi. He was betrothed to a woman née Chen. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Bangxian 諸邦憲, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhenbo, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-six and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan, a Department Magistrate; his grandfather was Tianxu; his father was Yu, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother, Bangzheng, was a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Qin. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Dashou 汪大受, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shuke, and he ranked thirty-eighth in the family’s male sibling generation. He was twenty-eight and was born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Shiwei; his father was Wenhua; and his mother was née Cheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Daxiang, and his younger brother was Dazan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 124th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Hong 謝紘, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Tianzhang, and he ranked twelfth in the family’s male sibling generation. He was twenty-seven and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu, a School Instructor; his grandfather was Hui, a tribute scholar; his father was Yin, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tong, and his younger brother was Gang. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanxi 王三錫, registered in Taicang Department, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household, was a native of Kunshan County, and was an supplementary student of the departmental school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruh uai [Ruhuai], and he ranked second among his brothers. He was twenty-five and was born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Hui, a Gentleman for Attending Affairs; his father was Shiyang, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Gu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Renyong, an upper-hall student; his younger brothers were Sanjie, Sangu, Sanpin, and Sansheng. He married a woman née Wu. He placed 126th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Zonggao, courtesy name Junbi, was registered in a military household of the Fushan Defense Battalion under the Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, with ancestral origins in Wan'an County, Jiangxi. A student of the Fushan County School, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, an honorary official for public benefactions; his grandfather was Heng, a county vice magistrate; his father was Tianxi, a department magistrate; and his mother was née Yu. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongyi, Zongfu, Zongzhou, Zongkui, and Zongji. He married a woman née Sun. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Jian, courtesy name Lianghan, was registered in an artisan household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzai, honorarily granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Guan, a prefect; and his father was Sheng, a surveillance vice commissioner. His mother, née Zou, was posthumously granted the title Lady (Ruren); his stepmothers were née Yu, who was granted the title Lady (Ruren), and née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Xiang, Ji (a student of the Directorate of Education), Zhi, and Pu; his younger brothers were Ke, Bang, and Ying. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Pei, courtesy name Bangjian, was registered in a military household in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan; his grandfather was Long; and his father was Zhen, an assistant instructor. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Qi, a prefectural vice prefect; Sui, a postal station master; Mao, a tribute student; and Yi. His younger brothers were Liu, Jing, Lü, and Shi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Song, courtesy name Rumao, was registered in a civilian household in Chuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the departmental school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather was Lian; his father was Jiang; and his mother was née Ni. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Gui, Chun, and Nan. He married a woman née Fan. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃卷〔貫錦衣衛，軍籍，湖廣麻城縣人，順天府學增廣生，治詩經，字景文，行二，年二十六，十月十六日生〕。曾祖文質，祖子華，父璲〔義官〕，母胡氏。具慶下，兄春，弟甲，娶武氏。順天府鄉試第十四名，會試第一百九十一名。

鄭慶〔貫福建福州府長樂縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字有章，行五，年四十三，四月初六日生〕。曾祖永昭，祖伯容，父孔信〔封户部主事〕，母卓氏〔贈安人〕，繼母林氏。慈侍下，兄文、靜〔訓導〕、賓〔訓導〕、寓，弟寅、憲〔刑部主事〕，娶李氏。福建鄉試第十五名，會試第二百四十名。
translation_en:
Wu Kui 吳逵, courtesy name Jinguang, was registered in a civilian household in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianji; his grandfather, Chungao; and his father, Chang, a county magistrate; his father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Zeng; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Xuan, Qian, Jiong, and Dao, and his younger brother was Shi; he married a woman née Xie and placed eighty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Juan 黃卷, courtesy name Jingwen, was registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Macheng County, Huguang; he was an added student at the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi; his grandfather, Zihua; his father, Sui, held the honorary title of Official of Righteousness; and his mother was née Hu; both parents were living; his elder brother was Chun and his younger brother was Jia; he married a woman née Wu and placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Xian 戴銑, courtesy name Zisheng, was registered in a military household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was an附? supplementary student at the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Anfu, posthumously granted the title of guard registrar; his grandfather was Duan, a guard registrar; his father was Sheng; and his mother was née Yuan; both parents were living; his elder brother was Zhao and his younger brother was Yi; he married a woman née Ye and placed ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Qing 鄭慶, courtesy name Youzhang, was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-three, and was born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhao; his grandfather, Borong; his father, Kongxin, was granted the title of secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his mother, née Zhuo, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Repose, and his stepmother was née Lin; his father was deceased and his stepmother living; his elder brothers were Wen, Jing (an assistant instructor), Bin (an assistant instructor), and Yu, and his younger brothers were Yin and Xian (a secretary in the Ministry of Justice); he married a woman née Li and placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黎晨〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣民籍，四川閬中縣人，縣學附學生，治詩經，字光啓，行四，年三十六，八月初九日生〕。曾祖真〔教諭〕，祖愷〔典史〕，父顥〔知州〕，母張氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄璉、瑛、璋，弟璜、昇、瓚、昺、琳、杲、果、璜，娶房氏。順天府鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百四十九名。

孫雲〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字從龍，行一，年三十四，九月初一日生〕。曾祖亮，祖俊〔典史〕，父泰，母倪氏。慈侍下，弟靈，娶金氏，繼娶徐氏。應天府鄉試第一百七名，會試第三百二名。

蔡雲程〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字亨之，行一，年三十六，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖廷貴，祖永昇〔太僕寺丞，贈徵仕郎、兵科右給事中〕，父潮〔布政司右布政使〕，母陳氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母洪氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，弟雲翰、雲翔、雲瑞，娶秦氏。浙江鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百四十七名。

陳詞〔貫直隸常州府江陰縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字子達，行二，年三十，九月初六日生〕。曾祖昇遠，祖玘〔義官〕，父鳳〔貢士〕，母吳氏，繼母胡氏。重慶下，兄情〔監生〕，弟編、力，娶吳氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十二名，會試第七十六名。
translation_en:
Li Chen 黎晨 was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was originally from Langzhong County, Sichuan. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guangqi; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Zhen, was a School Instructor; his grandfather, Kai, was a County Clerk; and his father, Hao, was a Department Magistrate. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lian, Ying, and Zhang; his younger brothers were Huang, Sheng, Zan, Bing, Lin, Gao, Guo, and Huang [the name 璜 appears twice, ?]. His wife was née Fang. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yun 孫雲 was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Conglong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Jun, was a County Clerk; his father was Tai, and his mother née Ni. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Ling. He married a woman née Jin and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yuncheng 蔡雲程 was registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Hengzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Tinggui. His grandfather, Yongsheng, was Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, posthumously granted the titles Gentleman for Attendant Service and Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War. His father, Chao, was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. His mother, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother, née Hong, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yunhan, Yunxiang, and Yunrui. His wife was née Qin. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ci 陳詞 was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zida; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shengyuan; his grandfather, Qi, held honorary official status; and his father, Feng, was a tribute scholar. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother née Hu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother, Qing, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Bian and Li [編力; division into names uncertain, ?]. His wife was née Wu. He placed 132nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳茂義〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字時卿，行二，年二十五，九月十三日生〕。曾祖志，祖倫，父鳳〔縣主簿〕，母魏氏。慈侍下，兄茂仁，弟茂禮，娶桂氏。浙江鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百七十四名。

translation_en:
Yang You, registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Jiande County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rucheng, he ranked twenty-third among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-six, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzheng, an unassigned official of the seventh rank; his grandfather was Dasheng, Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement (digong lang); his father was Xiang and his mother Lady Lang, both living; he married Lady Xu and subsequently another Lady Xu, and placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Shiwei, registered in a military household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongfu, he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shugao, his grandfather Jin, his father Ruqing, and his mother Lady Zou; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Lu, Dian, and Xian, he married Lady Li, and he placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Maoyi, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiqing, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Lun, his father Feng, a county Registrar, and his mother Lady Wei; his father had died and his mother was living, his elder brother was Maoren and his younger brother Maoli, he married Lady Gui, and he placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Fu, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guochang, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was forty-two, born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tinghou, his grandfather Qiande, his father He, his mother Lady Wu, and his stepmother another Lady Wu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Rao, Yangsu, and Yangqi, he married Lady Lü, and he placed fifty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Pan Fang, registered in the scholarly household category in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shushen; he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Hong was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, posthumously promoted through successive honors to Grand Master of the Palace and Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing. His grandfather Zhang was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner responsible for education, likewise posthumously promoted through successive honors to Grand Master of the Palace and Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing. His father Xizeng was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Works, concurrently serving as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Ye, was invested with the title Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sui, Jiong, Jin, Chun, and Ji; his younger brothers were Zhuo, Wei, Shao, Sui, Xuan, Yao, and Chuo. He married a woman née Qi. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Ding, registered in the commoner household category in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Changshu County and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jianhe; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xuan held an honorary office for longevity; his grandfather was Zongguang, his father was Rong, and his mother was née Tang. His mother alone survived. He married a woman née Ye. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Chen, registered in the commoner household category in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region and a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Xin held an honorary office for public benefaction; his grandfather Jin was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father Jin held an honorary office for public benefaction; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Min, and Huan. He married a woman née Du. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fei Yuan, registered in the wealthy household category in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang, and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rujin; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Bo'ang was posthumously appointed a District Magistrate. His grandfather Can was an Assistant Prefect, posthumously appointed Left Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. His father Kai was Grand Master for Administrative Service and Left Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. His mother, née Ren, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitable Service; his stepmother, née Li, was invested with the same title. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Mu, an Assistant Prefect, and Si. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Gou. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yi, registered in an artisan household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was an attached student of the Jiading County school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Chengzhi; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siming, his grandfather Hui, and his father Zhen; his legal mother was née Zhu and his birth mother née Ding. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xing and Qing, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brother was Xin. He married a woman née Hong. He ranked 128th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Luan was registered in an officer household in the Daning Front Guard and was a native of Yongnian County in the directly administered region. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yingzhi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the intercalary seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Neng was a Battalion Commander; his grandfather Ju was a Battalion Commander, posthumously granted the title General of Martial Virtue; and his father Shu was a Battalion Commander, granted the same title. His mother, née Li, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brother was E. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked 100th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 75th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wenyuan, registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Yangjing; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ronghai, his grandfather Hong was a County Registrar, his father was Zhuo, and his mother was née Cheng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Wenzhi and his younger brother Wenxiang. He married a woman née Jiang. He ranked 37th in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Biao, registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bangzheng; he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather Zihui held an honorary title for longevity; his father Mian held an honorary title for public beneficence; and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ye. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

安永清〔貫遼東廣寧衛，軍籍，衛學生，治書經，字汝澄，行一，年三十，十一月二十九日生〕。曾祖慶，祖順，父祿，母劉氏，繼母吉氏。重慶下，弟永潔、永康、永齡、永貞，娶龔氏。山東鄉試第二十三名，會試第三百八名。
translation_en:
Cao Bian, of Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zidong; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tianhua, posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Rendering Service; his grandfather was Wende, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Chi, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Luo, was invested as Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mian and Xie, and he married a woman née Deng. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Guxiang, of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in an official household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Luzhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather was Min; his father was Guan, a medical official; his father's former wife was née Fan; and his mother was née Qian. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Guzhen, a prefectural Registrar, and he married a woman née Hu. He placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Lie, of She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Weiguang; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather was Zuo, granted the honorary appointment of Investigating Censor; his father was Kai; and his mother was née Song. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Tao, a tribute scholar; Dian; Mo, a tribute scholar; Ran, a tribute scholar; and Xun. His younger brothers were Shu, Xu, Qian, and Shu. He married a woman née Fang and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Sun. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Yongqing, of Guangning Guard, Liaodong, was registered in a military household and was a guard school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Shun; his father was Lu; his mother was née Liu; and his stepmother was née Ji. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yongjie, Yongkang, Yongling, and Yongzhen, and he married a woman née Gong. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiong Guo 熊過 was registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, in the civilian register, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shuren; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-four, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Shilian, and his father Zai, a Prefect. His father's principal wife was née Wu, his successive stepmothers were née Fang and née Cheng, and his birth mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chi, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of an earlier examination, and Su; his younger brother was Zao. He married a woman née Huang. He placed ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Rushan 安如山 was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in the civilian register, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongjun, his grandfather Zuo, and his father Guo; both Zuo and Guo held honorary official status for charitable contributions. His mother was née Zhou, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rong and Liang; his younger brothers were Rupan, a student of the Imperial University, Rushi, Rujing, and Rugang. He married a woman née Guo. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Kelian 蔡克廉 was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in the civilian register, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Daoqing; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged nineteen, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, a Records Examiner; his grandfather was Kuan; and his father was You, a Professor. His father's former wife was née Bao, and his mother was also née Bao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kejing and Kecheng; his younger brother was Kexi. He was betrothed to a woman née Liu 留. He placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Ya 方涯 was registered in Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in the military register, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruji; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Bitong, who held honorary official status in recognition of longevity; and his father was Wen. His mother was née Hu, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Pu, a student of the Imperial University; his younger brother was Wei. He married a woman née Cao. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Wenzao 張文藻, courtesy name Meizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Shenzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the department school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Rang; his father, Han, a county vice magistrate; and his mother, née Zheng. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Wenyuan, a county vice magistrate; Wenhua; Wencui; Wenpu; Wenxuesheng [?], an Imperial University student; Wenqi; Wenshen; Wenqiang; and Wenzai. His younger brothers were Wenxian and Wenxuan. He married a woman née Wei. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Jia 薛甲, courtesy name Yingdeng, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Mi; his grandfather, Cong, an honorary official for charitable contributions; his father, Zhangxian; and his mother, née Xu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bu, Zhuo, Wu, and Ping. He married a woman née Shao. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Luan 趙鑾, courtesy name Minghe, was registered in a civilian household in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Bokai; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Ji; and his mother, née Sun. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Kai and Ke. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Huang 李䄓, courtesy name Zhongqian, was registered in a civilian household in Yongxing County, Chenzhou, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sikuan; his grandfather, Xiushi, a county magistrate granted the honorary title of secretary in the Ministry of War; his father, Yongfan, a county magistrate; and his mother, née Ma. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Cen and He [?; the division of these names is uncertain], the latter an Imperial University student; Xiang 亯, an acting instructor and provincial graduate (juren); Yi, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); Chu; Tiao; Zhu; Ti; and Tang. His younger brothers were Ji, Bu, and Shi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li 𤣱 [given-name pronunciation uncertain, ?], courtesy name Wenfu, was registered in an artisan household in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kongxian; his grandfather, Jiusi; his father, Weiguang; and his mother, née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Benren, courtesy name Cishan, was registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Pu; his father, Wenxiu; his mother, née Ma; and his stepmother, née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Benyi and Benxiao. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently women née Geng and née Shang. He ranked fifty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Shiping, courtesy name Yunsheng, was registered in a military household in Jiaohe County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zeng; his grandfather, An, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Xiu; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiwen, Shizai, Shixin, and Shixi. He married a woman née Cao. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Shixian, courtesy name Xinfu, was registered in a military household of the Yunnan Left Guard in Yunnan and was a native of Linchuan County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yongyu; his grandfather, Lin, held an honorary title for public beneficence; his father, Tong, was a subprefectural assistant magistrate; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Shizi, was an associate prefect; his younger brothers were Shigui, Shishi, Shiji, Shizhi, and Shigong. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He ranked fortieth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈愷〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字舜臣，行三，年三十六，十二月十五日生〕。曾祖思明，祖文浩〔壽官〕，父照，母陳氏。具慶下，兄泰、綬〔監生〕，弟鳴、悌、懷、忱，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十五名，會試第七十八名。
translation_en:
Wang Yangzheng, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bochun; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Yi, and his father Fan; his mother was née Ye. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yangxian, Yanghao (an Upper Hall student), and Yangsu. He married a woman née Peng. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cai, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuzhi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wencong (a Clerk in a suo office [?]), his grandfather Ji, and his father Han (a District Magistrate); his mother was née Wan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mu (an acting Assistant Instructor and provincial graduate) and Shu (术 [?]); his younger brother was He. He married a woman née Dong. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiwen, registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Songs. His courtesy name was Jingchun; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Libao, his grandfather Dunxin, and his father Xuan; his father's principal wife was née Xie, and his birth mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xizhou, Xiyi, Xiqing, Shizhao, Shizhang, Xiqi, and Xiyan (a Steward of Provisions); his younger brothers were Shixi and Ximeng. He married a woman née Li. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Kai, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Songs. His courtesy name was Shunchen; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siming, his grandfather Wenhao (an honorary official recognized for longevity), and his father Zhao; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tai and Shou (an Imperial University student); his younger brothers were Ming, Ti, Huai, and Chen. He married a woman née Chen. He placed 135th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yi, courtesy name Zhongzhan, was registered in a civilian household in Yongxing County, Chenzhou, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in his family and was forty-three years old, born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Sisu, officially commended as a charitable commoner; his grandfather was Rujin, an honorary official for charitable service; and his father was Yongsen, an honorary official on account of longevity. His mother was née Liao, and his stepmother née Chu. His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Dong, an Imperial University student; Dongdan [?], a county school Instructor and provincial graduate (juren); Sheng, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan) [?]; and Min. His younger brothers were Chu, Kun, Huang (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year), Bian, Man, Yu, Ri, Gao 杲, and Gao 槀. He married a woman née Cao. He placed seventy-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zhiwei, courtesy name Shiqi, was registered in a civilian household in Anyi County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked thirteenth in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Mianzheng, his grandfather Ming, and his father Zhongwen. His father's former wife was née Tu, his mother née Yu, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhiren, Zhidao, Zhian, and Zhijie. He married a woman née Shu. He placed eighty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Chunzhen, courtesy name Yiheng, was registered in a civilian household in Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Gongrong; his grandfather was Renjie, an Assistant Instructor; and his father was Tingzan. His mother was née Xie, and his stepmother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Chunlin, Chunxu, and Chuncui. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kaixian, courtesy name Bohua, was registered in a military household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zizhan, his grandfather Cong, and his father Chun, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His mother was née Wang. His mother alone survived. His younger brother was Jixian. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Zhi 蔣芝, registered in an official household of the Chengdu Front Guard in Sichuan and a native of Xianning County, Shaanxi, was an additional student at the Chengdu Prefectural School. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shihe. Seventh in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wenmin, a Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Jian, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Forthright Service; and his father was Bi, a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Yu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his mother, née Bai, was granted the same title. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wan, a Battalion Commander, Ying, an Assistant Prefect, and Kui; his younger brothers were Qin, Kui 蕢, Zhi, and Qian. He married a woman née Yu 于 and subsequently a woman née Song; the entry adds “betrothed” [?]. He placed thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Qing 鍾卿 was registered in a civilian household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maojing. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xu; his grandfather was Rui, an Instructor posthumously granted the office of Case Reviewer; and his father was Yunjin, an honorary official for public benefactions. His mother was née Qian and his stepmother née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ji, Xue, Hongdao, Hongmo, and Wen. He married a woman née Wei. He placed twenty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Guan 鄭觀 was registered in a civilian household in Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruzhong. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Zan, a tribute student posthumously granted the office of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Xuan, a Prefect. His mother, née Lan, was granted the title Lady of Tranquility. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qian, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Kun, a District Magistrate; his younger brothers were Jie, Fu, and Cui. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Wei 任洧 was registered in a civilian household in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qingzhi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the twentieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Fuchu, his grandfather Rui, and his father Jun; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhen and his younger brother Yuan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Zhifu 陳之輔, courtesy name Bofei, was registered in a civilian household in Yingshan County, Sui Subprefecture, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Run; his grandfather, Ji, held an honorary office for longevity; his father, Wei, was a National University student; and his mother was née Zhang 章. His mother alone was living. His elder brother, Zhiliang, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his younger brothers were Zhibi and Zhiheng. He married a woman née Zhang 張 and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Chen 樊臣, courtesy name Yizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order and was forty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shiguan, was posthumously appointed a Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather, Jin, was a Transport Commissioner; his father was Zuo; his mother was née Zhao; and his stepmother was née Wu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Kuang, Hui, and Po [?]. He married a woman née Wan. He placed sixty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shichong 魯時翀, courtesy name Xizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Huoqiu County, Shou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was a native of Taihe County, Jiangxi. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked eleventh in birth order and was forty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the intercalary ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Kui, was an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Tu; his father was Qiong; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Luan, Feng, Peng, He, Hong, Juan, Liang, An, Hui, and Pu; his younger brother was Yang. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shouqian 楊守謙, courtesy name Yunheng, was registered in a military household of Pengcheng Guard and was a native of Changsha County, Huguang. An additional student of the Shuntian prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second in birth order and was twenty-five years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fusheng. His grandfather, Chun, received the honorary appointment of Director in the Ministry of Revenue and was posthumously awarded the title Grand Master of Central Rectitude and the appointment of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His father, Zhixue, was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His father’s former wife, née Wang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Chen, was granted the same title. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Shouyu; his younger brothers were Shouyue, Shoumo, Shoulu, Shourang, Shoupu, Shouchu, and Shoujie. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳大壯〔貫河南河南府洛陽縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字子晋，行二，年二十六，六月十五日生〕。曾祖善，祖智〔衛知事〕，父龍〔訓導〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄大有〔貢士〕，娶劉氏。河南鄉試第一名，會試第一百九十二名。

王仲錦〔貫錦衣衛旗籍，江西吉水縣人，國子生，治詩經，字絅之，行一，年三十五，五月初八日生〕。曾祖永祺〔壽官〕，祖時阜〔封管軍百戶〕，父光明〔前副千戶〕，母廖氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，弟仲銓、仲鏞、仲鎡，娶龍氏。順天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第一百六十八名。

汪佀〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字克有，行百，年三十三，五月二十日生〕。曾祖景深，祖廷俊，父晏，母詹氏。具慶下，兄倬〔知州〕、佩、俸〔知縣〕、伻〔貢士〕、仟、何、俅〔貢士〕、脩，娶陸氏。江西鄉試第十名，會試第六十一名。

黃福〔貫直隸徽州府休寧縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字子謙，行三，年三十四，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖志昂，祖存耕，父以盛，母程氏。慈侍下，兄雷、全〔引禮舍人〕，娶程氏。應天府鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百七十名。
translation_en:
Chen Dazhuang, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in a civilian household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shan; his grandfather, Zhi, was a guard administrative clerk; his father, Long, was an assistant instructor; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Dayou, was a tribute student. He married a woman née Liu. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhongjin, courtesy name Jiongzhi, was registered in a bannerman household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Jishui County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yongqi, held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather, Shifu, was granted the title of company commander in charge of troops; his father, Guangming, was formerly a vice battalion commander; and his mother, née Liao, was granted the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongquan, Zhongyong, and Zhongzi. He married a woman née Long. He placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Si, courtesy name Keyou, was registered in a military household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked one hundredth in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingshen; his grandfather, Tingjun; his father, Yan; and his mother, née Zhan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhuo, a department magistrate; Pei; Feng, a county magistrate; Beng, a tribute student; Qian; He; Qiu, a tribute student; and Xiu. He married a woman née Lu. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Fu, courtesy name Ziqian, was registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiang; his grandfather, Cungeng; his father, Yisheng; and his mother, née Cheng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Lei and Quan, the latter a ceremonial usher. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed twenty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王納言〔貫河南信陽衛軍籍，襄城縣人，國子生，治詩經，字惟允，行一，年三十六，四月初三日生〕。曾祖貴，祖輪，父汝楫〔訓導〕，母李氏，繼母史氏、李氏。嚴侍下。弟納諫、納謨、納訓。娶黃氏。河南鄉試第十一名，會試第一百三十七名。

translation_en:
Jiang Guan, courtesy name Qizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhifang; his grandfather, Hu; and his father, Qing (an honorary official recognized for longevity). His father's former wives were both née Yang, and his birth mother was née Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bao, Lai, Bin, and Zhi. His wife was née Xie. He placed 124th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Cai, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Duo; his father, Hongji; and his mother, née Yan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Wu. He placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Nayan, courtesy name Weiyun, was registered in a military household of Xinyang Guard, Henan, and was a native of Xiangcheng County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Lun; and his father, Ruji (Assistant Instructor). His mother was née Li, and his stepmothers were née Shi and née Li. His father was living and his mothers deceased. His younger brothers were Najian, Namo, and Naxun. His wife was née Huang. He placed eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Boyue, courtesy name Qizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jizhang; his grandfather, Zipeng; his father, Jieda; his mother, née Xiong; and his stepmother, née Sun. He had living parents and grandparents. His elder brothers were Boxiu (Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission) and Boqin; his younger brothers were Boxiang and Bosheng. His wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.
