translation_en:
Wang Zhengsi 王正思 was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhongxing; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Tianxu, posthumously appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and subsequently granted the titles Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Special Advancement, Pillar of State, and Earl of Xinjian, concurrently Minister of War at Nanjing; his grandfather was Gun; his father was Shouli; and his mother was née Hua. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Zhengxin; his younger brothers are listed as Zhengxian, Zhengsi [?], Zhengzhong, Zhengmao, Zhengque, Zhengyu, Zhengyi, Zhengxian [?], Zhengzhi, Zhengyu, Zhengdang, and Zhenggan. The list repeats his own name and lists Zhengxian twice. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Xiangxian 鮑象賢 was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Fuzhi; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wanshan; his grandfather was Bangcan; his father was Guangzu; and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hu and Lian, and his wife was née Wang 汪. He placed one hundred fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Gao 吕高 was registered in a civilian household in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Siyi; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ang; his grandfather was Jing, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his father was Zongmei; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gu and Tang, and his wife was née Qian. He placed one hundred first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Yijun 莊一俊 was registered in a salt-service household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junfei; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yunsou; his grandfather was Zhen, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Wang; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Dao and Yizuo; his younger brothers were Long, Yongbin (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), Yiwen, Yifu, and Yizhen. His wife was née Wang 王. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡萬里〔貫陝西西安府咸寧縣，匠籍，府學生，治《詩經》，字伯明，行二，年二十七，八月十六日生〕。曾祖敏〔壽官〕，祖信〔縣丞〕，父貢珊，母李氏，繼母趙氏。具慶下，兄萬要，弟萬方〔貢士〕、萬春、萬邦、萬鎰、萬言、萬選、萬川、萬全、萬策。娶周氏。陝西鄉試第四十八名，會試第二十七名。

羅餘慶〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字道承，行一，年三十三，十二月二十一日生〕。曾祖宗讷，祖其卓，父體昌，母周氏。具慶下，弟重慶、德慶。娶周氏。江西鄉試第一百六名，會試第二百八十四名。
translation_en:
Zhao Wenhua, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuanshi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zeng, his grandfather Guangzong, his father Meng, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Song and Wenguang. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Xiang. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Gua, registered in a civilian household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shaoyi; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tingxi, his grandfather Xuan, a Prefectural School Instructor, his father Pu, and his mother née Peng; both parents were living. His elder brother was Sheng and his younger brother Tong. He married a woman née Wan. He placed sixty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Wanli, registered in an artisan household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boming; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Min, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Xin, a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Gongshan, his mother née Li, and his stepmother née Zhao. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother was Wanyao; his younger brothers were Wanfang, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Wanchun, Wanbang, Wanyi, Wanyan, Wanxuan, Wanchuan, Wanquan, and Wance. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yuqing, registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daocheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zongna, his grandfather Qizhuo, his father Tichang, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chongqing and Deqing. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed 106th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Fu, registered in a military household in Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhongli; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Yuan, an Imperial University student; his mother was née Shang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qing and Xiang, and his younger brother was Bi. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Peiling, registered in a civilian household in Xiangning County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yanfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather Wen had been honorarily invested as Assistant Prefect; and his father Jue was a Department Magistrate. His father's former wife, née Yan, had been posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yanling; his younger brothers were Yuling, a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort, and Yongling. He married a woman née Cui. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Lei, registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi, was a department school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kongjing; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather Gao and father Han each held honorary official status awarded for charitable contributions. His father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Han. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Ni and Lin, the latter a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort; his younger brothers were Ji, Fei, Pei, and Huo. He married a woman née Yan. He placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Dabin, registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Qinzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Yi, and his father Ding; his mother was née Cai. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Dajun, Dasu, and Da'an. He married a woman née Dai. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳瑺〔貫浙江杭州府錢塘縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字汝文，行十三，年四十二，二月初十日生〕。曾祖原敬〔贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，祖蕐〔贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，父誠〔通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，前母夏氏〔贈淑人〕，嫡母凌氏〔封淑人〕，生母張氏。永感下，兄璿〔府同知〕、璽、瑞、珎、琳、瑋〔義官〕、璠、璵、瑶〔中書舍人〕、瓊、玭〔行人司行人〕、珂，弟珊，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第三十名，會試第二百四十六名。

董雍〔貫四川成都府綿州民籍，州學生，治書經，字肅卿，行三，年三十三，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖昭〔學正〕，祖寅，父仲儒，母胡氏。永感下，兄庠〔監生〕、序，弟翼〔監生〕、爲，娶張氏。四川鄉試第十六名，會試第二百十六名。
translation_en:
Third class: 225 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Zhai Jing 翟鏡 was registered in a medical household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bingming, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong (described as “regular examination” [?]; posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor); his grandfather was Tinghui, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his father was Lian, an annual tribute student. His mother was née Meng. His mother alone survived, and he attended upon her. His elder brother was Yue and his younger brother was Lian. His wife was née Shao. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chang 吳瑺 was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruwen, and he ranked thirteenth among his brothers. He was forty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Yuanjing and grandfather Hua were both posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father Cheng held those same titles. His father's former wife, née Xia, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Virtue; his legal mother, née Ling, was invested with that title; and his birth mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xuan (Prefectural Vice Prefect), Xi, Rui, Zhen, Lin, Wei (Honorary Official), Fan, Yu, Yao (Secretariat Drafter), Qiong, Pin (Messenger of the Office of Transmission), and Ke; his younger brother was Shan. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yong 董雍 was registered in a civilian household in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Suqing, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-three years old, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, a School Director; his grandfather was Yin; his father was Zhongru; and his mother was née Hu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiang (an Imperial University student) and Xu; his younger brothers were Yi (an Imperial University student) and Wei. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Yingkui 孫應奎, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Wenqing; he ranked thirty-third among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Ding, his father Yue, and his mother née Tong. His parents and grandparents were living, and his wife was née Cen. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Datong 鄭大同, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Jiewu; he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shang (an honorary official honored for longevity), his grandfather Song, his father Xuan, and his mother née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Dabin; his younger brothers were Jiong (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year), Yue, Datian, Shao, Dahe, Wen, and Fei. His wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jue 楊爵, registered in Fuping County, Yao Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Boxiu; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Zheng, his father Pan, and his mother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jing, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Mi 沈謐, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan (an honorary official recognized for public beneficence), his grandfather Du (likewise an honorary official recognized for public beneficence), his father Fu, and his mother née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian and Ne. His wife was née Sheng, and he subsequently married another woman née Sheng. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫世祐〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字元吉，行十，年二十五，四月十四日生。〕曾祖高節，祖大成，父伯輝，母賴氏。具慶下，兄凱、顗、世祺，娶甘氏，繼娶范氏。江西鄉試第八十名，會試第三百二十名。

translation_en:
Zhou Ruyuan, courtesy name Wengui, was from Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, a prefect; his grandfather was Gai; his father was Zhong, a county magistrate; and his mother was née Hu. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Rufang, and his wife was née Luo. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Qiao, courtesy name Qianzhi, was from Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanmin; his grandfather was Zhihong; his father was Song, a prefectural school instructor; and his mother was née Luo. His father alone was still living. His younger brothers were Nanchou, Nanfan, Nanjia, Nanzheng, Nanji, Nanhua, and Nankai; his wife was née Ye. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Shiyou, courtesy name Yuanji, was from Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked tenth in birth order and was aged twenty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Gaojie; his grandfather was Dacheng; his father was Bohui; and his mother was née Lai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kai, Yi, and Shiqi. His wife was née Gan, and he subsequently married a woman née Fan. He placed eightieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhongfu, courtesy name Huaqing, was from Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and registered in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Hao, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Kai, a prefectural vice prefect; and his father was Lin, a ceremonial escort (consort of an imperial clanswoman). His father's principal wife was the County Princess of Longzhong, and his birth mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongli and Zhongxing; his wife was née Dai. He placed fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Shi, registered in Haifeng County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xida, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Lun, and his father Zan; his father's principal wife was Lady Qiang, and his birth mother was Lady Qiu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hua, and his younger brothers were Fan, Yun, Qiao, Ang, Yu, and Xiu. He married Lady Tang. He placed ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Yongbin, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Juncai, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yijin, his grandfather Yuanbi, his father Yan, and his mother Lady Xiao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Yongxu and Yijun (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), and his younger brother was Yonghui. He married Lady Li. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Guanghui, registered in Zichuan County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Huaguo, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Shan, and his father Jian; his father's principal wife was Lady Zhou, and his birth mother was Lady Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Guangyao, Guangcan, Guangbing, Guangye, Guangdun, Guangwei, and Guangxi. He married Lady Zhang and subsequently Lady Yu. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Liang, registered in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Suifu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Sheng, his father Yi, his mother Lady Zhang, and his stepmother Lady Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji (a County Chief Official), Chun, Zhang, Qi, and Pan; his younger brothers were Jin, Gong, Rang, and Du. He married Lady Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Feng, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bangji; he ranked fifth in birth order, was thirty-one, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Huan, Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission; his grandfather was Yugao; his father was Wanping; and his mother was née Liu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xuan, and his younger brothers were Yuan and Sui, the latter a Messenger in the Office of Transmission. His wife was née Ding. He placed thirty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Huan, registered in Changsha Guard, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuande; he ranked first in birth order, was forty-one, and was born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Xiang and grandfather Xuan were both Battalion Commanders; his father Tang was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hui, Huang, Fan, Yan, Kun, Jun, and Yan. His wife was née Ma. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongheng, registered in Wuyi County, Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jigao; he ranked third in birth order, was thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xu; his grandfather was Shu; his father was Fan; and his mother was née An. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zongdai, Zongzuo, and Zonghua. His wife was née Zhang. He placed one hundred twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Shisheng, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jiqing; he ranked ninth in birth order, was thirty-four, and was born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Kechang; his father was Mei, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Shihua, and his wife was née He. He placed seventy-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hou Ning, registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Huaide. Fourth in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Sen, was a Chief Clerk; his father was Lu, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing, Xiang, and Chong, and his younger brothers were Huan and Jian. His wife was née Yang. He placed fortieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Yigong, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was an added-quota student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Daozhuang. Second in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather was Ning, his father was Tong, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yizheng. His first wife was née Ou, and his subsequent wife was née Cai. He placed eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zixiao, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Chunshu. Second in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Tao, was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing. His grandfather, Yu, was honorifically appointed a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy and successively granted the posthumous titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel at Nanjing. His father, Yipeng, held the titles Grand Master for Fostering Virtue, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel at Nanjing. The maternal listing names a former mother, née Tang, followed by “successively granted the posthumous title Lady” and née Yao; the relationship of these phrases is unclear [?]. His legal mother was née Qian, successively invested with the title Lady of Chastity, and his birth mother was née Xue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Zizhong, and his wife was née Gu. He placed ninety-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zi, registered in Nanping County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Siyi. Second in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongyu, his grandfather was Zhongrong, his father was Zhen, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Hao, and his younger brothers were Si and Zhu. His wife was née Lin. He placed eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ge Shouli 葛守禮, courtesy name Yuli, was registered in a military household in Deping County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Youcai; his grandfather, Zhi, was a guard Registry Manager; his father was Huan, and his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shouyi, Shourang, and Shouzhen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Yue 危嶽, courtesy name Jizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Qianyang County, Yuanzhou Subprefecture, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Siming, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather, Shouxin, was an Instructor; his father, De, was an Assistant Prefect, and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chong, Jie, and Lü, and his wife was née Pan. He placed twenty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 306th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Huan 錢煥, courtesy name Shuhui, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His family birth-order designation is recorded as “bo liu” [?]. He was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Run, was a District Magistrate; his father was Gui, and his mother was née Ye. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yan and Can; his younger brothers were Yi, Ye, and Zhuo. His wife was née Ying. He placed fifty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Zhun 賈準, courtesy name Weiyi, was registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather was Lin; his father was Fu, and his mother was née Guo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jie and Dou, and his wife was née Tian. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王鉅 貫直隸徽州府婺源縣民籍 國子生
治書經字德卿行二年四十四月二十九日生
曾祖文亨 祖敬保 父齊玉 母黄氏
永感下 兄傑 娶程氏 繼娶張氏
應天府鄉試第四十一名 會試第二百二十五名
punctuated:
杜彰〔貫大寧前衛軍籍，順天府東安縣人，國子生，治詩經，字德明，行二，年四十，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖榮，祖裕，父福，母紀氏。慈侍下，兄彬，弟彩，娶譚氏。順天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第一百八十二名。

陳鉞〔貫留守前衛軍籍，直隸常熟縣人，國子生，治詩經，字惟鉉，行三，年三十九，四月初四日生〕。曾祖覺禮，祖俊〔贈奉直大夫、南京刑部員外郎〕，父瑜〔右長史，進階朝議大夫，前南京刑部郎中〕，母謝氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母石氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄銳、金，弟鎔、鏌、錠，娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第一百九十九名。

張勅〔貫直隸保定府完縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝欽，行一，年三十三，十二月十一日生〕。曾祖喜〔壽官〕，祖彬〔教授，封知州〕，父宦〔行太僕寺卿〕，前母劉氏〔贈孺人〕，母蔡氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，弟勃、勗、助、勉、勵，娶徐氏，繼娶孫氏。順天府鄉試第四十名，會試第二百十七名。

王鉅〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字德卿，行二，年四十，四月二十九日生〕。曾祖文亨，祖敬保，父齊玉，母黃氏。永感下，兄傑，娶程氏，繼娶張氏。應天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百二十五名。
translation_en:
Du Zhang, registered in a military household of the Daning Front Guard and a native of Dong’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deming, he was second in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Yu, his father Fu, and his mother née Ji; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Bin and his younger brother Cai, and he married née Tan; he placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yue, registered in a military household of the Liushou Front Guard and a native of Changshu County in Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weixuan, he was third in birth order, and he was thirty-nine years old, born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jueli; his grandfather Jun was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his father Yu was Right Chief Administrator, promoted in prestige rank to Grand Master for Court Discussion, and formerly a Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his mother, née Xie, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother, née Shi, was granted the same title; his father was deceased and his surviving mother living, his elder brothers were Rui and Jin and his younger brothers Rong, Mo, and Ding, and he married née Xu; he placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chi, registered in a military household of Wan County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruqin, he was first in birth order, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Xi held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather Bin was a Prefectural School Professor and was honorifically granted the title Department Magistrate; his father Huan was Minister of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud; his father’s former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Service, and his mother, née Cai, was granted the same title; his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brothers were Bo, Xu, Zhu, Mian, and Li, and he married née Xu and subsequently née Sun; he placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ju, registered in a civilian household of Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Deqing, he was second in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Wenheng, his grandfather Jingbao, his father Qiyu, and his mother née Huang; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Jie, and he married née Cheng and subsequently née Zhang; he placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

貫福建福州府閩縣民籍　府學生

貫直隸安慶府懷寧縣匠籍　國子生

曾祖元亨　祖淍〔義官〕　父信〔贈監察御史〕　母危氏〔贈孺人〕
永感下　兄楫〔監察御史〕　楫〔監生〕　弟橋〔醫官〕　桂　梗　檟　娶程氏

punctuated:
魯铣〔貫直隸揚州府江都縣軍籍，浙江黃巖縣人，府學生，治易經，字孚重，行四，年三十，二月十八日生〕。曾祖杲，祖宏，父𦚢，嫡母趙氏，生母張氏。具慶下，兄錦、銓，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百二十七名。

胡思忠〔貫直隸淮安府桃源縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字進之，行一，年四十，十一月十七日生〕。曾祖禮，祖瑛〔縣主簿〕，父鑑，母祝氏。永感下〔舊作具慶〕，娶夏氏。應天府鄉試第一百十四名，會試第一百二名。

朱德禎〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字必興，行一，年四十，二月十四日生〕。曾祖鑛，祖漢〔壽官〕，父璣，母陳氏。重慶下，弟德祿、德祚、德禧，娶謝氏。福建鄉試第二十五名，會試第二十八名。

丁祝〔貫直隸安慶府懷寧縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝和，行四，年四十三，六月十八日生〕。曾祖元亨，祖澗〔義官〕，父僖〔贈監察御史〕，母危氏〔贈孺人〕。永感下，兄楷〔監察御史〕、楫〔監生〕，弟格〔醫官〕、桂、梗、槓，娶程氏。應天府鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百四名。
translation_en:
Lu Xian 魯铣, courtesy name Fuzhong, was registered in a military household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Huangyan County, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather, Hong; and his father, 𦚢 [reading uncertain]. His father's principal wife was née Zhao, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin and Quan, and he married a woman née Chen. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Sizhong 胡思忠, courtesy name Jinzhi, was registered in a military household in Taoyuan County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Ying, a county Registrar; his father, Jian; and his mother, née Zhu. Both parents were deceased [the earlier text read “both parents living”]. He married a woman née Xia. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Dezhen 朱德禎, courtesy name Bixing, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Kuang; his grandfather, Han, held an honorary rank for longevity; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Delu, Dezuo, and Dexi, and he married a woman née Xie. He placed twenty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Zhu 丁祝, courtesy name Ruhe, was registered in an artisan household in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Songs, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanheng; his grandfather, Jian, held an honorary rank for public benefaction; his father, Xi, was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Wei, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kai, an Investigating Censor, and Ji, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Ge, a Medical Officer, Gui, Geng, and Gang. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

貫山東東昌府堂邑縣軍籍　國子生

曾祖廷　祖倫　父謙　母王氏

punctuated:
崔三畏〔貫直隸保定府蠡縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字敬父，行二，年三十三，八月十八日生〕。曾祖甫儀，祖翔〔署教諭，舉人〕，父岑〔知縣〕，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄三聘，娶段氏。順天府鄉試第五名，會試第二百九十九名。

王紳〔貫直隸河間府滄州，軍籍，州學生，治春秋，字子書，行二，年四十三，三月二十一日生〕。曾祖惟德〔縣主簿〕，祖吉，父國寧，母駱氏。具慶下，兄縉，弟績、統、緒，娶曾氏。順天府鄉試第七十一名，會試第三百九名。

舒國光〔貫江西廣信府弋陽縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字賓之，行六十九，年三十五，九月二十日生〕。曾祖旭澄，祖仲銓，父伯和，母吳氏。慈侍下，兄國泰、國用，弟國政、國相、國寶，娶鄭氏。江西鄉試第一百二十六名，會試第二百二十名。

邵新〔貫山東東昌府堂邑縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字循善，行三，年四十，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖通，祖倫，父謙，母王氏。永感下，兄儀、漢，娶吳氏。山東鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百二十一名。
translation_en:
Cui Sanwei, registered in Li County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked second in family order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fuyi; his grandfather, Xiang, was an acting county school instructor and a provincial graduate (juren); his father, Cen, was a county magistrate; and his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Sanpin, and his wife was née Duan. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shen, registered in Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zishu, he ranked second in family order, and he was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Weide, was a county registrar; his grandfather was Ji; his father was Guoning; and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin, his younger brothers were Ji, Tong, and Xu, and his wife was née Zeng. He placed seventy-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Guoguang, registered in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Binzhi, he ranked sixty-ninth in family order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xucheng; his grandfather was Zhongquan; his father was Bohe; and his mother was née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Guotai and Guoyong, his younger brothers were Guozheng, Guoxiang, and Guobao, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed 126th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Xin, registered in Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xunshan, he ranked third in family order, and he was aged forty, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Lun; his father was Qian; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi and Han, and his wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bai Shiqing, registered in Qinzhou, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruheng; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-four [?], born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Wenjin, an honorary official by reason of longevity; and his father was Guo, a county Registrar. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shiliang and Liangjue, and his younger brother was Shihui. His wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Duanyu, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shike; he ranked first in birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Yongji; and his father was Guan, an honorary official by reason of longevity. His mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Duanhuan, Duankui, Duanzao, Duanying, Duanshu, Duanyuan, and Duangan. His wife was née Liang. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Pu, registered in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dehong; he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the tenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Gui, and his father Quan; his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Han and Yuan; his younger brothers were Han, Yang, Ji, Jun, Cheng, and Hai. His wife was née Huang. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Xingzhi, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shuaiwu; he ranked seventh in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qian, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his grandfather was Liangchou; and his father was Yao, an annual tribute student. His mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xingcun, Xingchu, Xinggen, Xingyou, and Xingge; his younger brother was Xingquan. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Xuan, registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was an attached student of the county school who specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shunju; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shiming, his grandfather Youliang, his father Xianke, and his mother née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shu and Zun. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently women née Hua and Feng. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Zhongfu, registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouqing; he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Liang, and his father Hong; his legal mother was née Song and his birth mother née Cui. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Zhongshou. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed forty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kong Si, registered in an artisan household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zonglu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Yi, his father Zhang, a Police Chief, and his mother née Qiu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yi. He married a woman née Tian. He placed fourteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shunyuan, registered in a civilian household in Qingdu County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Guangling County, Shanxi, was a county-school student who specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bocai; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Han, an Assistant Magistrate; his father was Daben, an honorary official; and his mother was née An. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shunkai, Shunkui, Shunlong, and Shunmu. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed 109th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐湠〔貫浙江嚴州府淳安縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字景禹，行六，年四十六，九月二十日生〕。曾祖時，祖貢，父珪，母盧氏。永感下，兄濂〔貢士〕，弟滄，娶胡氏，繼娶齊氏。浙江鄉試第二十八名，會試第一百十七名。
translation_en:
Yang Bo 楊博, registered in a civilian household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a supplementary student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weiyue, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-one sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Chen; his grandfather, Xuan, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father, Shan, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Tian. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yun, Ke, Heng, Xin, Kai, Chen, Yu, Yi, Xu, Yi, Zao, and Xing, and his wife was née Duan. He placed twelfth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Jiugao 徐九皐, registered in a wealthy household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and originally from Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuanqing, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was twenty-six sui, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ang; his grandfather was Sui; his father, De, was Vice Commissioner of the Weaving and Dyeing Office under the Ministry of Works; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Jian 鍾鑑, registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi, was a supplementary student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Erzheng, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was thirty sui, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Hou, was a Prefectural Registrar; his grandfather was Yan; his father was Xun; his father's former wife was née Li; and his mother was née Qin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Yang, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, Quan, Yu, Luan, Ao, Fu, and Lian; his younger brothers were Zhu, a tribute student selected by special summons [?], Zhao, Rui, Liu, Hong, Zun, Qin, Diao, and Feng. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tan 徐湠, registered in a civilian household in Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jingyu, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was forty-six sui, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather was Gong; his father was Gui; and his mother was née Lu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother, Lian, was a tribute student, and his younger brother was Cang. His first wife was née Hu, and his subsequent wife was née Qi. He placed twenty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

林恕〔貫福建福州府長樂縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字道近，行三，年三十六，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖壮叔，祖在賓，父文秀，母張氏。具慶下，弟愈、忠、恩、端、方，娶陳氏，繼娶全氏、丁氏。福建鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百三十九名。

張忠〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字顯父，行二，年二十六，十一月初六日生〕。曾祖廣，祖政，父輗〔義官〕，母徐氏。慈侍下，兄恩，弟恕、思〔貢士〕，娶章氏。順天府鄉試第八十四名，會試第二百五十一名。

陶廉〔貫雲南曲靖衛軍籍，直隸當塗縣人，國子生，治書經，字敬甫，行三，年三十三，五月十一日生〕。曾祖鎔，祖深，父仲儒，母孫氏。具慶下，弟唐、賡，娶吳氏。雲貴鄉試第十一名，會試第七十一名。
translation_en:
Feng Bin, registered in an official household of Leizhou Guard, Guangdong, with supplementary registration in Haikang County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongxian; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gao, a Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Jian, an Assistant Prefect; his father was Lan, an Astrologer; and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mo, Gui, Zhen, Chun, and Quan, an Assistant Commander; his younger brothers were Tang, Cai, Bai, Shi, Dong, and Shao. His wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shu, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daojin; he ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhuangshu, his grandfather was Zaibin, his father was Wenxiu, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, Zhong, En, Duan, and Fang. His wife was née Chen; his subsequent wives were née Quan and née Ding. He placed thirty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhong, registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xianfu; he ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather was Zheng, his father was Ni, an honorary official, and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was En; his younger brothers were Shu and Si, the latter a tribute scholar. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Lian, registered in a military household of Qujing Guard, Yunnan, and originally from Dangtu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather was Shen, his father was Zhongru, and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tang and Geng. His wife was née Wu. He placed eleventh in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Xun, courtesy name Pingzhong, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twentieth in birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingheng, his grandfather Wen, his father Yu, and his mother née Lu; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Kun and his younger brother Tang; he married a woman née Zhu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jiusi, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Jiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Bi was an Instructor, posthumously awarded the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Zhonghui was a Prefect; his father Zonglun was an honorary official; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Jiucheng, and he married a woman née Mao. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Feng, courtesy name Junxi, was registered with the Guangxi Ceremonial Guard Office and was originally from Qingyuan County, Zhejiang. A student of the Guilin prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boliang, his grandfather Jian, his father Zhongju, and his mother née Xu; his mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Shen, an Instructor; Zhi [?]; Wei, an Assistant Instructor; and Yi, an Instructor. His younger brothers were Ru and Qiao, both tribute scholars (gongshi), and Wei, Qiu, and Bi. He married a woman née Wen and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed forty-third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Jie, courtesy name Yunxing, was registered in an artisan household in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan, his grandfather Qi, his father Kui, and his mother née Zhao; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Han, Shen, and Jie, and he married a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Wenfeng, courtesy name Gongyi, was registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Cuizhong; his grandfather was Mao, a School Instructor; his father was Anmin; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenying, Wenmao, and Wenlin, a Prefect; his younger brother was Wenlong. His wife was née Chen. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shen, courtesy name Yuanfu, was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was sixth in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ziming; his grandfather was Deming; his father was Qian; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hao, Jie, Fu, Wenming, and Cheng; his younger brother was Rong. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xianzong, courtesy name Zixiao, was registered in Puzhou, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Congyi; his grandfather was Tong; his father was Liangchen; and his mother was née Su. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Xianren. His wife was née Feng. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Mei, courtesy name Yihe, was registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Changji; his grandfather was Honggui; his father was Qiao; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingming, Tingyuan, and Tingcao; his younger brother was Tingjue. His wife was née Gao. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tian Ru, registered in Liaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shaosheng; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi; his grandfather, Mao; and his father, Shou, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Lü, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Pu, Shu, Ze (an Assistant Instructor), Chun, and Zhang. His wife was née Lü. He placed fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Ai, registered in Ningjin County, Zhao Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Tianzhang; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Qin; his father, Zheng; and his mother, née Kang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Zhan, and his younger brother was Dai. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sui Ye, registered in Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyun; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Hao; and his father, Zhongde, a Vice Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Ding, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yi, and his younger brothers were Yao, Yu, Wei, and Bing. His wife was née Jiang. He placed 111th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Renchun, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student at the prefectural school, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziren; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shisong; his grandfather, Yijin; and his father, Qi, an Assistant Prefect. His father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was also née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yidong. His wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Kang 趙康 was registered in Heyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weiji, and he ranked third in birth order. He was forty-one, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Gui, and his father Ying, an honorary official for longevity. His father’s former wife was née Lei, and his mother was née Che. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Feng and Luan, and his younger brother was Ning. His wife was née Jia. He placed forty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yunzong 林允宗 was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in an artisan household. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xizeng, and he ranked third in birth order. He was thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zaizhou, his grandfather Hongren, his father Minyi, and his mother née Huang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Yunsu, and his younger brothers were Yunji, Yunbi, and Yuncheng. His wife was née Huang; he subsequently married a woman née Gu. He placed eighty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yuanfu 趙元夫 was registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Qiren, and he ranked second in birth order. He was thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Zhuang, his father Sui, a tribute student, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengyou, a Secretary, and Qianfu; his younger brothers were Cuifu and Hengfu. His wife was née Tang. He placed fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rui 王銳 was registered in Xinyang Guard, Henan, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yangzhi, and he ranked sixth in birth order. He was forty, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Zhi, his father Hu, and his mother née Miao. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Jian, Zhen, Qin, Yue, and Gao. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Ye. He placed seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉瑜〔貫直隸大名府元城縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字貴卿，行一，年四十，十月十五日生〕。曾祖有源，祖增，父遷〔壽官〕，母張氏。具慶下，弟璣，娶傅氏。順天府鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百四十四名。

朱冕〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字文中，行二，年三十九，七月十三日生〕。曾祖仲方，祖寬，父廷輝〔縣丞〕，前母鄧氏，母余氏。慈侍下，兄顯、雲、良，娶徐氏。江西鄉試第十八名，會試第二百七十九名。

呂調羹〔貫山東東昌府濮州備禦所軍籍，湖廣嘉魚縣人，州學生，治禮記，字夢卿，行二，年三十二，正月初十日生〕。曾祖必勝，祖忠，父端〔知縣〕，母范氏。慈侍下，兄調陽，弟調元、調鼎、調琴、調笙、調竽，娶馮氏。山東鄉試第十名，會試第三百五名。

林山〔貫福建福州府長樂縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字士仁，行四，年三十五，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖綬，祖日用，父宗學，母陳氏。具慶下，弟阜、屺，娶黃氏。福建鄉試第六十名，會試第二百六名。
translation_en:
Liu Yu, registered in a civilian household in Yuancheng County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guiqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youyuan; his grandfather, Zeng; his father, Qian, held an honorary longevity title; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ji, and his wife was née Fu. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Mian, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenzhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongfang; his grandfather, Kuan; and his father, Tinghui, a County Vice Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Deng, and his mother was née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, Yun, and Liang, and his wife was née Xu. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Tiaogeng, registered in a military household at the Puzhou Defense Station, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a native of Jiayu County, Huguang, and a department school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Mengqing; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bisheng; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Duan, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Fan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Tiaoyang, and his younger brothers were Tiaoyuan, Tiaoding, Tiaoqin, Tiaosheng, and Tiaoyu. His wife was née Feng. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 305th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shan, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiren; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou; his grandfather, Riyong; his father, Zongxue; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fu and Qi, and his wife was née Huang. He placed sixtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

原寀〔貫陝西西安府華州蒲城縣軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字次寮，行二，年二十六，四月二十一日生〕。曾祖讓，祖格，父理，母竇氏。慈侍下，兄密，弟寵、宇，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第六十名，會試第八十一名。

魯守約〔貫廣東惠州府歸善縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子如，行二，年三十三，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖祖祐，祖羊保，父參，母崔氏。慈侍下，兄仁富，娶柯氏。廣東鄉試第六十四名，會試第一百六十一名。

饒中〔貫河南汝寧府光州固始縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字性甫，行三，年四十二，六月十七日生〕。曾祖伯肅，祖子貞，父景〔壽官〕，母汪氏。永感下，兄仁、禮、信、讓，弟正卿、申，娶李氏。河南鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百九十三名。
translation_en:
Xia Jun 夏浚 was registered in a civilian household in Yushan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Weiming and was twenty-fifth in family order, aged thirty-two, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Xi; his father was Ying, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chao, a seventh-rank prestige official, and Lan. He married a woman née Jiang. He ranked 178th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Cai 原寀 was registered in a military household in Pucheng County, Hua Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Ciliao and was second in family order, aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather was Ge; his father was Li; and his mother was née Dou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Mi, and his younger brothers were Chong and Yu. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shouyue 魯守約 was registered in a military household in Guishan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ziru and was second in family order, aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuyou; his grandfather was Yangbao; his father was Can; and his mother was née Cui. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Renfu. He married a woman née Ke. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Zhong 饒中 was registered in a civilian household in Gushi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Xingfu and was third in family order, aged forty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bosu; his grandfather was Zizhen; his father was Jing, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ren, Li, Xin, and Rang, and his younger brothers were Zhengqing and Shen. He married a woman née Li. He ranked thirty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Meng Bin, registered in Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the department school; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Kongzhang, ranked first in family order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather, Gao, and father, Han, both held honorary office for public benefaction; his father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ni; his younger brothers were Lei (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year), Ji, Fei, Pei, and Huo. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Cheng. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zonglu, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Xizeng, ranked fourth in family order, and was aged thirty-five, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gao, his grandfather Ding, and his father Zheng, who held honorary office for public benefaction; his father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zongwei and Zongru, and his younger brother was Zongdao. He married a woman née Ye. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Zai, registered in Shehong County, Tongchuan Department, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Zikun, ranked second in family order, and was aged forty-seven, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingde, who held honorary office conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Ying, his father Ji, and his mother née Yuan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Gai, and his younger brothers were Yu and Hui. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Fengchun, registered in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the county school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Renfu, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengde, his grandfather Han𣊵 [second character's reading uncertain], who held honorary office conferred for longevity, his father Xuangong, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xulong, and his younger brother was Fengyang. He married a woman née Hong. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

高大經〔貫直隸順德府任縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字以仁，行八，年二十八，六月二十一日生〕。曾祖泰，祖達，父時〔監生〕，母吳氏。慈侍下，兄拱，娶駱氏。順天府鄉試第六十九名，會試第六十六名。

李鳳〔貫四川敘州府富順縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字鳴叔，行二，年三十六，七月初三日生〕。曾祖繼宗〔贈文林郎、翰林院編修，加贈中憲大夫、南京太常寺少卿，累贈通議大夫、禮部右侍郎〕，祖本〔資善大夫、南京禮部尚書〕，父文昌〔府照磨〕，母胡氏。嚴侍下，兄夔，娶嚴氏。四川鄉試第二十五名，會試第一百五十一名。

柳本明〔貫河南汝寧府光州光山縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字誠甫，行一，年四十四，六月十七日生〕。曾祖純一，祖仲昇，父春，嫡母邵氏，生母胡氏。永感下，娶童氏。河南鄉試第五名，會試第一百八十名。
translation_en:
Gao Dajing 高大經, courtesy name Yiren, was registered in a civilian household in Ren County, Shunde Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was eighth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai; his grandfather, Da; his father, Shi, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Gong, and his wife was née Luo. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan 張環, courtesy name Mengxun, was registered in a military household of the Xi’an Right Escort Guard in Shaanxi. A student of the Chang’an County school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Fu; his father, Jie; and his mother, née Wang 汪. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yue, and his wife was née Wang 王. He placed fifty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Feng 李鳳, courtesy name Mingshu, was registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Jizong, was posthumously granted the titles Gentleman of Literary Distinction and Hanlin Academy Junior Compiler, subsequently Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing, and ultimately Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Rites. His grandfather, Ben, was Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Rites at Nanjing; his father, Wenchang, was a prefectural Record Keeper; and his mother was née Hu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his wife was née Yan. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Benming 柳本明, courtesy name Chengfu, was registered in a military household in Guangshan County, Guang Zhou, Runing Prefecture, Henan. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chunyi; his grandfather, Zhongsheng; and his father, Chun. His father's principal wife was née Shao, and his birth mother was née Hu. His parents were deceased. His wife was née Tong. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.
