translation_en:
Xie Kun 謝崑, courtesy name Zhongpu, was registered in a civilian household in Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He was Assistant Instructor at the county school of Jinhua, Zhejiang, and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. First in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyao; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Hao; his mother, née Chen; and his stepmother, née Lin. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Yue, Yan, and Chong. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Rumo 邢如默, courtesy name Xuanfu, was registered in a military household in Linyi County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Zheng, a Department Magistrate; his father, Pu; and his mother, née Xu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Han, Shuang, Jia, Ruyue, Ruchu, and Ruyi. His wife was née Zhao. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Zhou 方舟, courtesy name Shiji, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a supplementary student at the prefectural school and specialized in the Classic of Documents. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sida; his grandfather, Bao; his father, Jian; and his mother, née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Pan, Meng, and Ban. His wife was née Pan. He placed one hundred second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ruji 李汝楫, courtesy name Jiqing, was registered in a military household in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, a student of the Imperial University; his grandfather, Yongnian, a Granary Commissioner; his father, Shoujing, a Prefect; and his mother, née Gong. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Ruyu, Rubi, and Ruxi. His wife was née Yang. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Bengu, courtesy name Daoshen, was registered in a military household in Shangcheng County, Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather Congli and father Dayong both held honorary offices conferred for longevity. His mother was née Xia and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother Benli was a Registrar in a Regional Military Commission; his younger brothers were Benlian and Benzong, the latter an honorary official recognized for public benefactions. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked seventy-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shitai, courtesy name Daoheng, was registered in a military household of Zhending Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Gaoyou Subprefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, his grandfather Kemu, and his father Xian; his mother was née Zhao and his stepmother née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shiyong and Shixi. He married a woman née Shuai. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Donghai, courtesy name Shiguan, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the thirteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deyu, his grandfather Xuemao, and his father Zongzhong, a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Ou, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Dongshan. He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Guanghua, courtesy name Daoyun, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liji, his grandfather Yuanfeng, and his father Gui; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother Guangming was a tribute student; his younger brothers were Guangchun, Guangjing, and Guangyan. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Lin. He ranked twenty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Feng 劉鳳 was registered in a civilian household in Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Mingqi, ranked second among his brothers, and was forty sui old, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Wen, his father Bangfu, and his mother née Xu; his parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Luan, and his younger brothers were Peng, Fu, and Ti 鶙. He married a woman née Tao. He placed eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hongfan 周洪範 was registered in a military-and-civilian household in Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and was originally from Anfu County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Bochen, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-nine sui old, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Yuejian, his father Shizhao, and his mother née Deng; his father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Shu 錢澍 was registered in a military household in Xinghe Battalion under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission and was originally from Qian'an County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Tianze, ranked second among his brothers, and was forty sui old, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather De, his father Bi, and his mother née Wu; his parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Cheng and his younger brother Pao 泡. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yanxin 李延馨 was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yunming, ranked third among his brothers, and was thirty-two sui old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhimei; his grandfather Zhu was a District Magistrate, and his father Xuan was a District Vice Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Feng; both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Yanying and Yanchang, and his younger brother Yankang was a government-stipend student. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張明道〔貫湖廣黃州府羅田縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字希程，行一，年四十九，三月十七日生〕。曾祖克敬，祖昇，父大洪，母毛氏。永感下，娶章氏。湖廣鄉試第六名，會試第六十五名。

白賁〔貫四川潼川州民籍，國子生，治春秋，字亨甫，行四，年四十，八月二十一日生〕。曾祖普榮，祖父明，父雲漢，母何氏。具慶下，兄采、賛，弟貢、貴、賢、贄、賓，娶鄭氏。四川鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百五十名。

陳蕙〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，府學生，治春秋，字邦馨，行五，年三十，十二月初二日生〕。曾祖霽曾，祖崇瑞，父朗〔上林苑監典簿〕，前母吳氏，母朱氏。慈侍下，兄芳〔監生〕、蒼，弟荌、蕃、英、滿、壽、福，娶張氏。福建鄉試第四十四名，會試第二百八十五名。
translation_en:
Cao Kui, courtesy name Lüzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changshu County. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Liangyi; his grandfather was Min, an honorary official; his father was Zhengang; and his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Di, Yuan, and Xuan, and his wife was née Gu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mingdao, courtesy name Xicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Luotian County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Kejing; his grandfather was Sheng; his father was Dahong; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Bi, courtesy name Hengfu, was registered in a civilian household in Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Purong; his grandfather was Fuming [?]; his father was Yunhan; and his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cai and Zan, and his younger brothers were Gong, Gui, Xian, Zhi, and Bin. His wife was née Zheng. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hui, courtesy name Bangxin, was registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jizeng; his grandfather was Chongrui; and his father was Lang, Registrar in the Directorate of Imperial Parks. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Fang, an Imperial University student, and Cang; his younger brothers were An, Fan, Ying, Man, Shou, and Fu. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Gao 張鎬, registered in Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shujing. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Xiang, his father Xian, and his mother née Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin, and his younger brothers were Zi, Yue, Quan, and Lu. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Quan 李全, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qiuquan. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and was born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zisen, his grandfather Jie, and his father Dengshi; his father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hua and Mei, and his younger brothers were Cui and Xin. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Qiangao 石遷高, registered in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Qianfu. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Caiguang, his father Da, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Qianyao. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Qi. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Tinggui 任廷貴, registered in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junjue. First in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Zhide, his father Jing, and his mother née Yang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Tingzan, Tingqi, and Tingbao. He married a woman née Qu, followed by successive wives née Xue, Liu, and Li. He ranked nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

張鳧〔貫山東登州府萊陽縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字羽卿，行三，年三十，三月十八日生〕。曾祖鎧，祖鵬，父瑄〔義官〕，母蕭氏，繼母李氏。慈侍下，兄鸞〔州吏目〕、鳳〔典膳〕、麒〔典膳〕、麟〔典膳〕，弟鷗、鶱，娶李氏。山東鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百九十六名。

閻鄰〔貫山東兗州府東平州，軍籍，州學生，治書經，字德甫，行一，年三十，十二月初八日生〕。曾祖貴，祖宏，父縉〔運司經歷〕，前母張氏、王氏，母胡氏，繼母楊氏。具慶下，兄儒，娶管氏。山東鄉試第六十六名，會試第六十四名。

陳珪〔貫廣東高州府化州，民籍，州學生，治詩經，字禹成，行四，年二十七，十二月初九日生〕。曾祖舍存，祖清，父禧〔國子監助教〕，前母王氏，母吳氏。具慶下，兄玘、珫，弟琚，娶張氏。廣東鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百十四名。

林繼皐〔貫福建福州府閩縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字允謨，行十八，年二十四，七月三十日生〕。曾祖皛〔知縣〕，祖楙，父一能，母陳氏。具慶下〔兄繼元、繼賢、繼貞，知縣；弟繼昭、繼治、繼祿，貢士；繼大、繼立，娶秦氏〕。福建鄉試第三十九名，會試第一百二十四名。
translation_en:
Zhang Fu 張鳧, registered in Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yuqing, he ranked third in the family, and he was thirty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Peng, and his father Xuan, an honorary official; his mother was née Xiao and his stepmother née Li. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Luan, a subprefectural clerk; Feng, Qi, and Lin, each a steward of food; his younger brothers were Ou and Xian, and his wife was née Li. He placed forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Lin 閻鄰, registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Defu, he ranked first in the family, and he was thirty years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Hong, and his father Jin, a registrar in a Salt Distribution Commission; his father's earlier wives were née Zhang and née Wang, his mother was née Hu, and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ru, and his wife was née Guan. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Gui 陳珪, registered in Huazhou Subprefecture, Gaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yucheng, he ranked fourth in the family, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shecun, his grandfather Qing, and his father Xi, an instructor in the Directorate of Education; his father's earlier wife was née Wang and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi and Chong, his younger brother was Ju, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Jigao 林繼皐, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yunmo, he ranked eighteenth in the family, and he was twenty-four years old, born on the thirtieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiao, a county magistrate, his grandfather Mao, and his father Yineng; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiyuan, Jixian, and Jizhen, a county magistrate; his younger brothers were Jizhao, Jizhi, Jilu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Jida, and Jili, and his wife was née Qin. He placed thirty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖胜〔贈翰林院檢討〕 祖恭〔州判累封通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕 父天敘〔嘉議大夫都察院右副都御史陞俸一級〕 母郝氏〔累封恭人〕

punctuated:
許勉仁，貫四川成都左護衛官籍，雙流縣人，國子生。治易經，字希顏，行二，年二十六，三月初八日生。曾祖誠，祖琛〔贈禮部員外郎〕，父淳〔右布政使，進階正奉大夫、正治卿〕，嫡母郝氏〔封宜人〕，生母王氏。具慶下，兄恩〔典膳〕，弟依仁，娶徐氏，繼娶何氏。四川鄉試第二十四名，會試第二百六十一名。

黃訓，貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生。治書經，字學古，行四，年四十，六月十八日生。曾祖仲旭，祖文器，父琛，母殷氏。永感下，兄謨、詔、誥〔監生〕，弟表、勅、譚、誨、誡、記、誦、訴、詢，娶胡氏，繼娶孫氏。應天府鄉試第十一名，會試第六十四名。

趙鯤，貫山東兖州府東平州壽張縣民籍，國子生。治詩經，字于南，行一，年四十，四月初十日生。曾祖伯通，祖榮，父奎〔縣主簿〕，母陳氏。永感下，弟永康〔典膳〕、鱣，娶路氏，繼娶劉氏。山東鄉試第十四名，會試第一百八十四名。

寇陽，貫山西太原府榆次縣軍籍，縣學附學生。治詩經，字體乾，行一，年二十六，五月十七日生。曾祖玘〔贈大理寺右評事〕，祖恭〔州判，累封通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，父天敘〔嘉議大夫、都察院右副都御史，陞俸一級〕，母郝氏〔累封恭人〕。重慶下，弟𨹧、阡、隅、階、隆、阼、附、陸、防、隨、陛、陞、阺、陌、陳，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。山西鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百十九名。
translation_en:
Xu Mianren was registered in an official household of the Chengdu Left Escort Guard in Sichuan and was a native of Shuangliu County. He was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xiyan. Second in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Chen, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; and his father was Chun, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, advanced to the ranks of Grand Master for Upright Service and Minister for Orthodox Governance. His father's principal wife was née Hao, granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was En, a Director of Provisions, and his younger brother was Yiren. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née He. He ranked twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xun was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xuegu. Fourth in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxu, his grandfather was Wenqi, his father was Chen, and his mother was née Yin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mo, Zhao, and Gao, the last a student of the Imperial University. His younger brothers were Biao, Chi, Tan, Hui, Jie, Ji, Song, Su, and Xun. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Sun. He ranked eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Kun was registered in a civilian household in Shouzhang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. He was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yunan. First in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Botong, his grandfather was Rong, his father was Kui, a County Registrar, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yongkang, a Director of Provisions, and Zhan. He married a woman née Lu and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kou Yang was registered in a military household in Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. He was an supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tiqian. First in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the seventeenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, posthumously granted the title of Right Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. His grandfather was Gong, a Subprefectural Assistant Judge, successively granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Tianxu, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, whose salary had been raised by one grade. His mother was née Hao, successively granted honorary titles culminating in Lady of Respect. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ling (𨹧), Qian, Yu, Jie, Long, Zuo, Fu, Lu, Fang, Sui, Bi, Sheng, Di, Mo, and Chen. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently another woman née Wang. He ranked thirty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
丘峻〔貫直隸蘇州府嘉定縣匠籍，國子生，治易經，字惟陟，行九，年四十二，六月十三日生。〕曾祖震，祖剛，父鉞，嫡母顧氏，繼嫡母張氏、周氏，生母王氏。具慶下，兄山，弟嶠，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第一百名，會試第二百三十四名。

楊沔〔貫應天府句容縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字東之，行一，年四十四，十一月十八日生。〕曾祖隆一，祖茂林，父惠〔縣主簿〕，嫡母趙氏，繼嫡母陳氏，生母杜氏。慈侍下，娶曹氏，繼娶曹氏、許氏，繼聘孔氏。應天府鄉試第一百八名，會試第一百五十八名。

孫濟〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣匠籍，國子生，治書經，字以道，行三，年四十六，正月初九日生。〕曾祖保，祖昌，父綱〔縣丞〕，前母沈氏，母劉氏。慈侍下，兄澄、溥，娶周氏，繼娶張氏。浙江鄉試第四十名，會試第三十名。

丘汝良〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字民牧，行五，年三十六，十月初一日生。〕曾祖福〔贈嘉議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，祖鼎〔贈儒林郎布政司理問〕，父鈿〔知州〕，母李氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄濟〔鴻臚寺序班〕、民望〔聽選官〕、民器〔貢士〕、民秀、民範〔知府〕、民清，弟汝賢〔刑部主事〕、民偉、汝器、汝方，娶吳氏。江西鄉試第一百二十七名，會試第二百二十六名。
translation_en:
Qiu Jun 丘峻, registered in an artisan household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weizhi; he ranked ninth in family order and was forty-two years old, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Gang, and his father Yue; his father's principal wife was Lady Gu, the subsequent principal wives were Lady Zhang and Lady Zhou, and his birth mother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shan and his younger brother Jiao. He married Lady Zhang. He placed one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Mian 楊沔, registered in a military household in Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dongzhi; he ranked first in family order and was forty-four years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Longyi, his grandfather Maolin, and his father Hui, a County Registrar; his father's principal wife was Lady Zhao, the subsequent principal wife was Lady Chen, and his birth mother was Lady Du. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married Lady Cao, subsequently married another Lady Cao and Lady Xu, and was subsequently betrothed to Lady Kong. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Ji 孫濟, registered in an artisan household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yidao; he ranked third in family order and was forty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bao, his grandfather Chang, and his father Gang, a County Vice Magistrate; his father's former wife was Lady Shen and his mother was Lady Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Cheng and Pu. He married Lady Zhou and subsequently Lady Zhang. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Ruliang 丘汝良, registered in a civilian household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Minmu; he ranked fifth in family order and was thirty-six years old, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fu was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Ding was posthumously granted the titles Gentleman for Scholarly Service and Judicial Officer in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father Dian was a Department Magistrate, and his mother, Lady Li, was granted the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji, an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial; Minwang, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Minqi, a tribute student; Minxiu; Minfan, a Prefect; and Minqing. His younger brothers were Ruxian, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; Minwei; Ruqi; and Rufang. He married Lady Wu. He placed 127th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Dong, courtesy name Zhiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Shouzhang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was originally from Ningxia Guard, Shaanxi. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yancheng; his grandfather, Zheng; his father, Xian, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chun, Huai, and Mei. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Bi, courtesy name Maodong, was registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An added-quota student at the Huai’an County school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twentieth in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Xiu, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Zhen, was a tribute student (gongshi), posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his father, Wenzuan, was a retired Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, advanced in rank to Grand Master of Central Compliance. His mother, née Wu, was invested with the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhi, and his younger brothers were Xun, Jiong, and Shi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Cheng, courtesy name Bangmei, was registered in a military household in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bicheng; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Tai; his mother, née Wu; and his stepmother, née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jun, Jie, and Wei. He married a woman née Li and subsequently another woman née Li. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chu Bao, courtesy name Guangchu, was registered in an official household of Huaiyuan Guard in the directly administered territory and was originally from Yanshi County, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged forty, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, a Company Commander; his grandfather, Yong; his father, Gao; and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jun, Guan, Huan, Qian, and Bin. He married a woman née Pan and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Ding, registered in a military household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Jingyu, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was twenty-five, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijie; his grandfather was Kun, an honorary official by virtue of longevity; his father was Yongqi; his mother was née Sun, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tang, Luan, Huang, Quan (a Judge), and Lu. He married a woman née Lu. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Dong, registered in a commoner household in Chaocheng County, Pu Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Boyang, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-one, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Shan, his father Rulong, and his mother née Shang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Nan and Xi. He married a woman née Yu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Zhuo, registered in an official household in Long Subprefecture, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yunzhang, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was thirty-six, born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiu, posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Xuan, an Instructor, likewise posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his father was Zhongyu, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. His father's former wife, née Zhong, was posthumously granted the title Lady; his mother, née Yuan, was granted the title Lady. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ru (a Company Commander), You (a District Magistrate), Fu (a tribute scholar), and Feng (a Judge). He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yongcheng, registered in a military household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Sizhen, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-three, born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wantong; his grandfather was Chongli; his father was Jia, an honorary official by virtue of philanthropy; his father's former wife was née Peng, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qicheng and Yancheng, and his younger brothers Shangcheng and Wencheng. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Man 江滿, courtesy name Qianzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Qiming, an honorary official for public benefaction; his grandfather was Zhengxing; his father was Chaozhong; and his mother was née Yang. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Yuan, Chao, and Pan; his younger brothers were Zhi, a tribute student, Gun, and Yi. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Sicheng 歐思誠, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a civilian household in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Lianjiang County, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Record of Rites; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bao, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Jun; his father was Hongde, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Meng. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brother was Sigong, a tribute student; his younger brothers were Sizhong, Sixiao, Sixian, a tribute student, Siqi, a ninth-rank prestige official, Sijin, Sifa, and Siyuan. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Gongsheng 陳公陞, courtesy name Boju, was registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the prefectural Confucian school, he specialized in the Record of Rites; he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Xian, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; his father was Zhengmo; and his mother was née Zhang, officially honored as a chaste widow. His mother alone survived. He married a woman née Zhao. He ranked first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Fu 賀府, courtesy name Yingbi, was registered in a military household in Weinan County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Odes; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ben; his grandfather was Ru; his father was Cang, an agricultural official; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lai. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked forty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

倪嵩〔貫直隸太平府當塗縣，匠籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字中卿，行三，年三十六，十一月十六日生〕。曾祖泰，祖讓，父璋，前母李氏，母蔣氏。慈侍下，兄山、岳，弟崞，娶謝氏。應天府鄉試第一百名，會試第二百七十八名。

高懋〔貫四川重慶府合州銅梁縣，民籍，縣學生，治《禮記》，字惟德，行四，年三十八，三月二十九日生〕。曾祖福源，祖振〔省祭官〕，父相〔壽官〕，母胡氏。具慶下，兄志、慧、愈，娶王氏。四川鄉試第四十八名，會試第三百十三名。
translation_en:
Liu Shu 劉塾, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruxue, he ranked seventh in his family, and he was thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Kai, was a Medical Officer; his father was Bing, his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xun 壎. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Zhan 丁湛, registered in Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ziyi, he ranked nineteenth in his family, and he was thirty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huiyuan, his grandfather was Yihong, his father was Shangyu, and his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Yuan 淵, an Imperial University student, Yuan 源, Yi, Gai, and Pan; his younger brothers were Rui, Wen, Wei, Shi, and Xun. He married a woman née Liu. He placed 153rd in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Song 倪嵩, registered in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongqing, he ranked third in his family, and he was thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather was Rang, and his father was Zhang; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Jiang. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Shan and Yue, and his younger brother was Guo. He married a woman née Xie. He placed 100th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Mao 高懋, registered in Tongliang County, He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Weide, he ranked fourth in his family, and he was thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan; his grandfather, Zhen, was a Provincial Sacrificial Official; his father, Xiang, held the honorary title of Longevity Official; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Hui, and Yu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Longxi, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziqian, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hao, Gentleman for Rendering Service; his grandfather was Shi, an Investigating Censor; his father was Fu, an Imperial University student awaiting selection for office; and his mother was née Wang. His father alone was living. His elder brother, Duanxi, was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Zhixi and Yuanxi. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shangning, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Tingde, and he ranked eleventh among his brothers. He was twenty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yonggong, his grandfather Shouxiang, his father Shixun, and his mother née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhou. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ning, registered in Jianning County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chende, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Juqian, his grandfather Shixian, his father Qitao, and his mother née Rao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jun, Bin, Yi, Yin, and Fu. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Bi, registered with the Guangxi Princely Guard, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the Lingui County school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Heyu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Ju, his father Jing, and his mother née Zuo. His mother alone was living. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Ru, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zichun, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-five, born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was 𨌆 [reading uncertain]; his grandfather was Mu; his father was Jie; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yi, and his wife was née Ma. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fu, registered in a military household in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dewei, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shan; his grandfather was Wen, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Zhou; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rui, and his younger brothers were Qin, Quan, Hao, and Zhen. His wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Shou, registered in a military household of the Ningxia Central Garrison Guard in Shaanxi and a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongpei, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-one, born on the first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather was Yu; his father was Chun, a Steward of Food; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brother was Tong. His wife was née Wang, and he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed forty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Nian, registered in a military household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Gongfu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-seven, born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Yichu; his father was Qing, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Quan, a tribute scholar, and Qian. His wife was née Cheng. He placed seventieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳昌福〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字子隆，行三，年三十，十月初一日生〕。曾祖正諒，祖必弘，父主思，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄昌典、昌積，弟昌載、昌祉。娶曽氏。江西鄉試第二十三名，會試第一百九十五名。

黃正色〔貫直隸常州府江陰縣，軍籍，無錫縣人，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字士尚，行四，年二十九，十二月十二日生〕。曾祖以衡，祖萱，父坤〔義官〕，母周氏，繼母薛氏。具慶下，兄正宗、正心、正諫，弟正守。娶蕭氏。應天府鄉試第一百十七名，會試第三十五名。
translation_en:
Guo Congpu 郭從朴, registered in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenbo. Listed as first in birth order, he was forty-three years old and was born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zong; his grandfather, Zhao, was an Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father, Dongshan, was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in the Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Mao, was granted the title of Ruren (Lady). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Congsu and Congzhai; his younger brothers were Congcai, Congjie, Congrong, and Congzhi. He married a woman née Qu and subsequently women née Sun and Liu. He ranked sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guan Huaili 管懷理, registered in Linyi County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yichu. First in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bing, his grandfather Fang, and his father Pu; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Huaien, Huaide, and Huaiyi. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Changfu 陳昌福, registered in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zilong. Third in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhengliang, his grandfather Bihong, and his father Zhusi; his mother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Changdian and Changji; his younger brothers were Changzai and Changzhi. He married a woman née Zeng. He ranked twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhengse 黃正色, registered in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a native of Wuxi County. He was an added student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shishang. Fourth in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yiheng, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Kun, an honorary official for public beneficence. His mother was née Zhou, and his stepmother was née Xue. Both parents were recorded as living. His elder brothers were Zhengzong, Zhengxin, and Zhengjian; his younger brother was Zhengshou. He married a woman née Xiao. He ranked 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Yunqian, registered in Yazhou, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruyi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Ming, was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Upright Service and had been a Vice Director acting as Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; his father, Fang, was a Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. He had grandparents and parents living; his younger brother, Yunzhi, was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his wife was née Shao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ji, registered in Liquan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruji, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Han; his grandfather, Shan, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Di; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Chong, his younger brothers were Hong and Ze, and his wife was née Jin. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Lian, registered in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuansu, he ranked fourteenth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Jun, was a Department Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Shunzhong; his father, Wenxian, was an Assistant Instructor; his father’s former wife was née Long, and his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Gang, Shou, Zhen, and Ji, his younger brother was Wei, and his wife was née Cao. He placed twentieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Fu, registered in Jingmen Department, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruqing, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged eighteen, born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun; his grandfather, Qing, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Tiangui, was an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Wang. He had grandparents and parents living; his elder brother was Ru, his younger brothers were Zuo, Hua, and Zhu, and he was betrothed to a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

葉洪〔貫直隸德州衛，官籍，浙江餘姚縣人，國子生，治書經，字子源，行六，年三十四，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖亮〔百戶〕，祖韶〔百戶〕，父瑁，母王氏。具慶下，兄樹，弟濟、梅，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第十三名。
translation_en:
Cao Ru, registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rulin; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Yan, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his father, Jian, was a county Registrar. His mother was née Bi, and his stepmother née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ze, a County Vice Magistrate; Ji, an Official for Righteousness; and Run. His younger brother was Shi. He married a woman née Liang. He placed thirty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chaolie, registered in a military household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Changqing; he ranked third in his family and was aged forty, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Can; his grandfather, San; and his father, Tong, a Post Station Master. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jing and Jie, and his younger brothers Jiang and Sheng. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventeenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Wenguang, registered in a military household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongshi; he ranked tenth in his family and was aged fifty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Sida; and his father, Lu. His mother was née Xiong, and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Wenbi. His younger brothers were Wenkui, Wenqing (a District Magistrate), Wenzhen, Wengeng, Wensheng, Wenxian, Wenhua, and Wenbo. He married a woman née He. He placed eleventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Hong, registered in an official household of Dezhou Guard in Zhili and originally from Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Liang, and grandfather, Shao, were both Company Commanders. His father was Mao, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shu, and his younger brothers Ji and Mei. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

馬書林〔貫陝西西安府高陵縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子約，行一，年三十五，三月初三日生〕。曾祖傑，祖文質，父憲，母齊氏。重慶下，弟桂林、儒林、雲林、易林、田林、鳳林，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百七十三名。

translation_en:
Zhu Yong, registered in a military household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang, and a native of Guiyang County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Mingsheng; he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Fengyin, and his father Shouhua, who held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his mother was née Yan. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhao, and his younger brothers were Song and Yi. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Tan. He placed sixty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chong, registered in a civilian household of Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongde; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhaohu, a prestige official of the seventh rank; his grandfather was Fu, who held an honorary title bestowed for longevity; his father was Ke, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jing and Hong. He married a woman née Xie. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Shulin, registered in a civilian household of Gaoling County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyue; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the third day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Wenzhi, and his father Xian; his mother was née Qi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Guilin, Rulin, Yunlin, Yilin, Tianlin, and Fenglin. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, registered in a civilian household of Xi’an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zaishu; his birth order is recorded as “he san” [?], apparently third. He was aged forty-one and born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shiyan, his grandfather Xi, and his father Wenhui; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiong and Rong. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently women née Zhang and née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Xi, registered in a military household of Shouzhou Guard in Zhili, was a student of the Shouzhou school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boqing; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Li, his father Lian, and his mother née Li. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chao and Pei, and his wife was née Gu. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Yingyue, registered in a civilian household of Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xianzhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-seven years old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sanqi, his grandfather Jianjun, his father Zhengyong, and his mother née Mao. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His wife was née Xiao. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bing, registered in an official household of Changhuai Guard at Zhongdu and originally from Daye County, Huguang, was a student of the Fengyang County school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jinchu; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, a Company Commander; his grandfather was Jing, his father Hui, and his mother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Jing, Bian, and Xu. His wife was née Tang, and he was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Cao. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Rudi, registered in a civilian household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunzhi; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Tinglan, his grandfather Yun, his father Bi, and his mother née Qian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruzhao, a student of the Imperial University, Rudou, Rudeng, Rulun, Rujiang, and Ruhan. His wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉鳳翔〔貫陝西西安後衛軍籍，咸寧縣學生，治易經，字仲集，行三，年三十七，正月十六日生〕。曾祖凱，祖俊，父璧，母趙氏。永感下，兄鳳儀、鳳鳴，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。陝西鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百九十二名。

張鵬翼〔貫河南開封府歸德州虞城縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字雲程，行十二，年三十二，四月二十八日生〕。曾祖清，祖三恭，父文勝〔壽官〕，母周氏。具慶下，兄繼宗、聰、喜、表、秀、名、進、廷、高、子良、子賢，弟鵬摶，娶劉氏，繼娶王氏。河南鄉試第六十九名，會試第一百四名。

李士文〔貫福建福州府連江縣民籍，湖廣嘉魚縣學教諭，治易經，字在中，行四，年四十三，四月二十日生〕。曾祖澤，祖彥偉，父景，母謝氏。慈侍下，兄希文，娶董氏。福建鄉試第九十名，會試第九十名。

戴繼〔貫山東兖州府曹州曹縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字淑似，行一，年三十四，七月十九日生〕。曾祖海，祖敖，父昂，母邵氏。具慶下，弟綵、縝、緇，娶周氏。山東鄉試第五十二名，會試第二百九十一名。
translation_en:
Liu Fengxiang, registered in a military household of the Xi’an Rear Guard in Shaanxi, was a student of the Xianning County school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongji; he ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Jun, his father Bi, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fengyi and Fengming. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently married another woman née Wang. He placed fifty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Pengyi, registered in a civilian household in Yucheng County, Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the county school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuncheng; he ranked twelfth in birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Sangong, his father Wensheng (holder of an honorary official title for longevity), and his mother née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jizong, Cong, Xi, Biao, Xiu, Ming, Jin, Ting, Gao, Ziliang, and Zixian; his younger brother was Pengtuan. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiwen, registered in a civilian household in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was Instructor at the Jiayu County school in Huguang and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zaizhong; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged forty-three, and was born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ze, his grandfather Yanwei, his father Jing, and his mother née Xie. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Xiwen. He married a woman née Dong. He placed ninetieth in both the Fujian Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Ji, registered in a military household in Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shusi; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Ao, his father Ang, and his mother née Shao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cai, Zhen, and Zi. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed fifty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
金清〔貫應天府上元縣民籍，直隸崑山縣人，國子生，治詩經，字廉夫，行二，年三十四，五月二十二日生〕。曾祖通，祖銀〔封監察御史〕，父冕〔中憲大夫、按察司副使〕，嫡母吳氏〔封安人〕，生母周氏。慈侍下，兄潾、沂、淳、湏、淇，弟湛、瀚〔監生〕，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第二十三名，會試第九十八名。

章允賢〔貫直隸池州府青陽縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字汝愚，行一，年二十七，十月二十日生〕。曾祖伯通〔義官〕，祖叔直〔義官〕，父果〔監生〕，母汪氏。具慶下，弟允中、允元、允亨，娶方氏。應天府鄉試第一百名，會試第九名。

張裕〔貫直隸蘇州府嘉定縣匠籍，長洲縣人，國子生，治書經，字士弘，行一，年四十一，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖源〔壽官〕，父翺，母陳氏，繼母鄭氏。具慶下，弟祐、表、禮，娶宗氏。應天府鄉試第二十二名，會試第二十四名。

茅宰〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣民籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字治卿，行一，年二十六，四月二十八日生〕。曾祖肅，祖鎧，父璘，母陳氏。重慶下，娶胡氏。浙江鄉試第六名，會試第七十三名。
translation_en:
Jin Qing, courtesy name Lianfu, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Yin, was honorifically invested as Investigating Censor; and his father, Mian, was Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father's principal wife, née Wu, was invested as Lady of Peace; his birth mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Lin, Yi, Chun, Xu [?], and Qi; his younger brothers were Zhan and Han, the latter an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yunxian, courtesy name Ruyu, was registered in a civilian household in Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Botong, and grandfather, Shuzhi, both held honorary official status for philanthropy; his father, Guo, was an Imperial University student, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yunzhong, Yunyuan, and Yunheng. He married a woman née Fang. He ranked one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yu, courtesy name Shihong, was registered in an artisan household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was a native of Changzhou County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in family order, aged forty-one, and born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Yuan, held honorary official status for longevity; his father was Ao, his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Zheng. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were You, Biao, and Li. He married a woman née Zong. He ranked twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Zai, courtesy name Zhiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in family order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Su, his grandfather was Kai, his father was Lin, and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. He married a woman née Hu. He ranked sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
郝維嶽〔貫四川敘南衛軍籍，敘州府學附學生，治詩經，字叔望，行一，年二十七，十一月二十三日生〕。曾祖文先，祖忠，父廷相，母牟氏。永感下，弟維崑、維崙，娶李氏。四川鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百四十九名。

羅虞臣〔貫廣東廣州府順德縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字熈載，行一，年二十四，十二月初九日生〕。曾祖子品，祖孫璣，父昌冑，母黃氏。重慶下，弟虞牧、虞工、虞獻，娶張氏。廣東鄉試第十四名，會試第一百十三名。

王鎬〔貫直隸永平府灤州民籍，國子生，治易經，字宗周，行五，年三十二，十月初六日生〕。曾祖貴〔壽官〕，祖暹，父璋〔縣丞〕，母李氏。慈侍下，兄鎧、鑰、鉦〔貢士〕、鏞，弟錮、鍔、鍊，娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百八十一名。

卞偉〔貫四川敘州府宜賓縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子充，行一，年四十二，三月十一日生〕。曾祖如圭〔壽官〕，祖紀〔縣主簿〕，父鳳來，母劉氏，繼母廖氏。永感下，兄俊，弟价、倣、傑、佐、佑、信、儉、儼，娶尹氏，繼娶姚氏、周氏。四川鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百三十三名。
translation_en:
Hao Weiyue, courtesy name Shuwang, was registered in a military household of Xunan Guard, Sichuan, and was an additional student of the Xuzhou Prefectural School. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wenxian; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Tingxiang; and his mother, née Mou. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Weikun and Weilun, and his wife was née Li. He placed fifty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yuchen, courtesy name Xizai, was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was twenty-four years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zipin; his grandfather, Sunji; his father, Changzhou; and his mother, née Huang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yumu, Yugong, and Yuxian, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fourteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hao, courtesy name Zongzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked fifth in birth order, and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather, Xian; his father, Zhang, a County Vice Magistrate; and his mother, née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Kai, Yue, Zheng (a tribute scholar), and Yong; his younger brothers were Gu, E, and Lian. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Wei, courtesy name Zichong, was registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was forty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Rugui, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather, Ji, a County Registrar; his father, Fenglai; his mother, née Liu; and his stepmother, née Liao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jun, and his younger brothers were Jie, Fang, Jie, Zuo, You, Xin, Jian, and Yan. His wife was née Yin; he subsequently married women née Yao and née Zhou. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖某 祖欽〔義官〕 父霖 母吳氏
慈侍下 兄來卿 弟來賓 來寅 來俞 來朋 來王 來元 來庭 娶錢氏
順天府鄉試第一百三十三名 會試第五十九名
punctuated:
高進〔貫錦衣衛校籍，直隸崑山縣人，國子生，治詩經，字維藎，行一，年二十九，五月初八日生〕。曾祖顯，祖恮〔光祿寺署正，贈工部郎中〕，父嶼〔按察司副使〕，母康氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第八名，會試第二十五名。

王與齡〔貫山西平陽府鄉寧縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字受甫，行三，年二十二，七月初五日生〕。曾祖豪，祖文〔封承德郎、通判〕，父爵〔知州〕，前母閻氏〔贈安人〕，母李氏。重慶下，兄延齡、培齡〔同科進士〕，弟永齡，娶高氏。山西鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百名。

陳捷〔貫福建福州府長樂縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字仲遵，行三，年三十七，正月初二日生〕。曾祖思眾，祖宗禮，父孟約，母林氏。嚴侍下，娶鄒氏。福建鄉試第八十一名，會試第八十二名。

范來賢〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字昌國，行一，年二十八，八月初三日生〕。曾祖基，祖欽〔義官〕，父霖，母吳氏。慈侍下，兄來卿，弟來相、來賓、來俞、來朋、來王、來元、來庭，娶錢氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十三名，會試第五十九名。
translation_en:
Gao Jin 高進 was registered in a guardsman household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Kunshan County, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Weijin and ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Quan, was an Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Works; his father, Yu, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Kang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He placed eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuling 王與齡 was registered in a civilian household in Xiangning County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Shoufu and ranked third among his brothers. He was twenty-two, born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Wen, was granted the titles Gentleman for Maintaining Virtue and Assistant Prefect; and his father, Jue, was a Department Magistrate. His father's former wife, née Yan, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Repose; his mother was née Li. Members of both his parents' and grandparents' generations were living. His elder brothers were Yanling and Peiling, the latter a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort; his younger brother was Yongling. His wife was née Gao. He placed thirty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jie 陳捷 was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zhongzun and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-seven, born on the second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Sizhong, his grandfather Zongli, his father Mengyue, and his mother née Lin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His wife was née Zou. He placed eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Laixian 范來賢 was registered in a military household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Changguo and ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-eight, born on the third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather, Qin, held honorary official status for public benefaction; his father was Lin, and his mother née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Laiqing; his younger brothers were Laixiang, Laibin, Laiyu, Laipeng, Laiwang, Laiyuan, and Laiting. His wife was née Qian. He placed one hundred thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳大綸〔貫廣西南寧衛軍籍直隸舒城縣人 府學生 治書經字伯言行二年二十六十一月十九日生〕

punctuated:
沈鐸〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字時振，行一，年四十，九月初一日生〕。曾祖信，祖瑒〔壽官〕，父璇，母邵氏。具慶下，弟鉞、鑰、鍇，娶宋氏。浙江鄉試第八十二名，會試第一百七十四名。

皇甫汸〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字子循，行三，年二十六，八月十二日生〕。曾祖通，祖信〔贈禮部員外郎〕，父錄〔知府〕，母黃氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄冲〔貢士〕、涍〔貢士〕，弟濂，娶沈氏，繼聘談氏。應天府鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百九十名。

陳大綸〔貫廣西南寧衛，軍籍，直隸舒城縣人，府學生，治書經，字伯言，行二，年二十六，十一月十九日生〕。曾祖亮，祖清，父琚〔判官〕，母蔡氏，繼母李氏。慈侍下，兄大經〔貢士〕，弟大紀、大綱，娶李氏。廣西鄉試第四十二名，會試第八十五名。

吳孟祺〔貫山東兗州府寧陽縣，軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字元壽，行一，年三十二，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖寛，祖仲德〔壽官〕，父偉〔教授〕，母陳氏。永感下，弟孟祿、孟雄，娶石氏。山東鄉試第三名，會試第四十七名。
translation_en:
Shen Duo 沈鐸, courtesy name Shizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather was Yang 〔honorary official for longevity〕; his father was Xuan; and his mother was née Shao. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Yue, Yue 鑰, and Kai, and his wife was née Song. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huangfu Fang 皇甫汸, courtesy name Zixun, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili; he was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Xin 〔posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites〕; his father was Lu 〔Prefect〕; and his mother was née Huang 〔granted the title Lady of Suitability〕. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Chong 〔tribute student〕 and Xiao 〔tribute student〕, and his younger brother was Lian; he married a woman née Shen and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Tan. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dalun 陳大綸, courtesy name Boyan, was registered in a military household of the Nanning Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Shucheng County, Zhili; he was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather was Qing; his father was Ju 〔Administrative Assistant〕; his mother was née Cai; and his stepmother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Dajing 〔tribute student〕, his younger brothers were Daji and Dagang, and his wife was née Li. He placed forty-second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Mengqi 吳孟祺, courtesy name Yuanshou, was registered in a military household in Ningyang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather was Zhongde 〔honorary official for longevity〕; his father was Wei 〔Prefectural School Instructor〕; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased; his younger brothers were Menglu and Mengxiong, and his wife was née Shi. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜朝聘貫山東兗州府東平州東阿縣民籍 國子生
